Moses had defeated him along with the Midianite chiefs Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, who were princes allied with Sihon and lived in the land. ²² Among those killed by the Israelites was Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, who was put to the sword. ²³ The Jordan formed the western boundary of the Reubenites. These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Reubenites by their clans. ²⁴ Moses also gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad according to its clans. ²⁵ Their territory included Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer near Rabbah;

²⁶ and from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpah and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the territory of Debir; ²⁷ and in the valley, Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon — the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon. The Jordan formed the boundary along the eastern shore of the Sea of Kinnereth. ²⁸ These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Gadites by their clans. ²⁹ Moses also gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh — this was the possession of half the tribe of Manasseh by their clans. ³⁰ Their territory extended from Mahanaim through all of Bashan — the entire kingdom of Og king of Bashan — including all sixty towns of Jair in Bashan;

³¹ and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan, were given to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh — to half the descendants of Machir by their clans. ³² These are the territories Moses had distributed as inheritances on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan across from Jericho. ³³ But Moses gave no inheritance to the tribe of Levi; the LORD God of Israel is their inheritance, as he had promised them.

[Chapter 14] ¹ These are the territories that the Israelites received as their inheritance in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the tribal families of Israel distributed to them. ² Their inheritances were assigned by lot to the nine and a half tribes, as the LORD had commanded through Moses. ³ Moses had already given the two and a half tribes their inheritance east of the Jordan, but he gave the Levites no inheritance among the rest. ⁴ The descendants of Joseph had become two tribes — Manasseh and Ephraim — and no share of the land was given to the Levites except cities to live in, along with their surrounding pasturelands for their livestock and property. ⁵ The Israelites carried out the LORD's command to Moses and divided the land.

⁶ The men of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God about you and me at Kadesh Barnea. ⁷ I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy out this land, and I brought back an honest report. ⁸ My fellow spies made the hearts of the people melt with fear, but I followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly. ⁹ On that day Moses swore, saying, The land you walked on will be your inheritance and your children's forever, because you followed the LORD your God wholeheartedly. ¹⁰ Now then, the LORD has kept me alive these forty-five years, just as he promised, since the day he said this to Moses while Israel wandered in the wilderness. Here I am today, eighty-five years old.

¹¹ I am still just as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out. I have the same strength for battle now as I had then. ¹² So give me this hill country the LORD promised me that day. You heard then that the Anakites were there and their cities were large and fortified — but if the LORD is with me, I will drive them out just as he said. ¹³ Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance. ¹⁴ So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite ever since, because he followed the LORD God of Israel wholeheartedly. ¹⁵ Hebron's former name was Kiriath Arba, named after Arba, the greatest man among the Anakites. And the land had rest from war.

[Chapter 15] ¹ The allotment for the tribe of Judah by its clans extended down to the territory of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin in the far south. ² Their southern boundary started from the southern tip of the Dead Sea, ³ ran south of the Scorpion Pass, continued to Zin, went up south of Kadesh Barnea, past Hezron, up to Addar and curved around to Karka. ⁴ From there it passed along to Azmon and went out to the Wadi of Egypt, ending at the sea. That is your southern boundary. ⁵ The eastern boundary was the Dead Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan. The northern boundary began at the bay at the mouth of the Jordan,

⁶ went up to Beth Hoglah and continued north of Beth Arabah; then it went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben. ⁷ From the Valley of Achor the boundary went up toward Debir, then turned north toward Gilgal, which faces the Pass of Adummim south of the ravine, continued to the waters of En Shemesh, and ended at En Rogel. ⁸ Then the boundary went up through the Valley of Ben Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite ridge — that is, Jerusalem. From there it climbed to the top of the hill on the western edge of the Hinnom Valley, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim. ⁹ From there the boundary curved from the hilltop to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, came out near the towns of Mount Ephron, and then curved to Baalah, which is Kiriath Jearim. ¹⁰ From Baalah the boundary turned westward to Mount Seir, continued along the northern slope of Mount Jearim — that is, Kesalon — went down to Beth Shemesh, and passed along to Timnah.

¹¹ The boundary continued to the northern slope of Ekron, curved to Shikkeron, passed along to Mount Baalah, and went out to Jabneel, ending at the sea. ¹² The western boundary was the coastline of the Mediterranean Sea. These are the boundaries on all sides for the clans of Judah. ¹³ In keeping with the LORD's command to Joshua, Caleb son of Jephunneh was given a portion among the people of Judah — Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron. (Arba was the father of Anak.) ¹⁴ From there Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. ¹⁵ From there he marched against the people living in Debir, which was formerly called Kiriath Sepher.

¹⁶ Caleb said, I will give my daughter Achsah in marriage to the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher. ¹⁷ Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah in marriage. ¹⁸ One day when she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb asked her, What do you want? ¹⁹ She answered, Give me a blessing — you've given me land in the Negev; give me springs of water too. So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs. ²⁰ This is the inheritance of the tribe of Judah by its clans.

²¹ The cities farthest south belonging to the tribe of Judah toward the border of Edom were Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur, ²² Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah, ²³ Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan, ²⁴ Ziph, Telem, Bealoth, ²⁵ Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (that is, Hazor),
²⁶ Amam, Shema, Moladah, ²⁷ Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet, ²⁸ Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah, ²⁹ Baalah, Iim, Ezem, ³⁰ Eltolad, Kesil, Hormah,

³¹ Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah, ³² Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon — twenty-nine towns in all, with their surrounding villages. ³³ In the western foothills: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, ³⁴ Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, ³⁵ Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,

⁴¹ Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah — sixteen towns with their villages. ⁴² Libnah, Ether, Ashan, ⁴³ Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, ⁴⁴ Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah — nine towns with their villages. ⁴⁵ Ekron, with its surrounding settlements and villages.

⁴⁶ West of Ekron, all the towns near Ashdod with their villages; ⁴⁷ Ashdod with its towns and villages; Gaza with its towns and villages as far as the Wadi of Egypt, and the coastline of the Mediterranean Sea. ⁴⁸ In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, ⁴⁹ Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (that is, Debir), ⁵⁰ Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,

⁵¹ Goshen, Holon, and Giloh — eleven towns with their villages. ⁵² Arab, Dumah, Eshan, ⁵³ Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah, ⁵⁴ Humtah, Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron), and Zior — nine towns with their villages. ⁵⁵ Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,

⁵⁶ Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, ⁵⁷ Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah — ten towns with their villages. ⁵⁸ Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor, ⁵⁹ Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon — six towns with their villages. ⁶⁰ Kiriath Baal (that is, Kiriath Jearim) and Rabbah — two towns with their villages.

⁶¹ In the wilderness: Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah, ⁶² Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi — six towns with their villages. ⁶³ As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the people of Judah could not drive them out, and the Jebusites live alongside the people of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

[Chapter 16] ¹ The allotment for the descendants of Joseph began at the Jordan near Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, and went up through the wilderness into the hill country of Bethel. ² From Bethel it went to Luz and continued to the border of the Arkites at Ataroth, ³ then went westward to the territory of the Japhletites as far as the territory of Lower Beth Horon and on to Gezer, ending at the sea. ⁴ So the descendants of Joseph — Manasseh and Ephraim — received their inheritance. ⁵ The territory of the Ephraimites by their clans was as follows: the boundary of their inheritance on the east ran from Ataroth Addar to Upper Beth Horon,

⁶ and the boundary continued to the sea. On the north it ran from Michmethath eastward; the boundary turned south from there to Taanath Shiloh and passed by it on the east to Janoah. ⁷ From Janoah it went down to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho, and came out at the Jordan. ⁸ From Tappuah the boundary went westward to the Kanah Ravine and ended at the sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim by its clans. ⁹ The separate towns set aside for the Ephraimites were within the inheritance of Manasseh, all the towns with their villages. ¹⁰ They did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; to this day the Canaanites live among the Ephraimites and are required to do forced labor.

[Chapter 17] ¹ The allotment was made for the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph's firstborn. Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, was a warrior, so Gilead and Bashan were given to him. ² The remaining descendants of Manasseh received allotments by their clans — the families of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph by their clans. ³ Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. ⁴ They came before Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun and the leaders, saying, The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our male relatives. So in accordance with the LORD's command, Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers. ⁵ Manasseh received ten shares of land, in addition to the lands of Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan,

⁶ because Manasseh's daughters received an inheritance along with his sons. The land of Gilead went to the rest of Manasseh's sons. ⁷ The territory of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath near Shechem. The boundary ran southward from there to the inhabitants of En Tappuah. ⁸ Manasseh had the land of Tappuah, but the town of Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the Ephraimites. ⁹ The boundary then went down to the Kanah Ravine. The towns south of the ravine belonged to Ephraim, though they were within the territory of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh ran along the north side of the ravine and ended at the sea. ¹⁰ The land to the south belonged to Ephraim and the land to the north belonged to Manasseh, with the sea as the western border. The two tribes met in Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

¹¹ Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also had Beth Shean and its surrounding settlements, Ibleam and its settlements, and the inhabitants of Dor, En Dor, Taanach, and Megiddo, along with their settlements — three hill districts. ¹² Yet the Manassites were unable to drive out the inhabitants of those towns, and the Canaanites were determined to stay in that region. ¹³ When the Israelites grew stronger, they subjected the Canaanites to forced labor but did not drive them out completely. ¹⁴ The descendants of Joseph complained to Joshua, Why have you given us only one allotment and one portion as our inheritance? We are a numerous people, for the LORD has blessed us greatly. ¹⁵ Joshua answered, If you are so numerous and the hill country of Ephraim is not big enough for you, go up into the forest and clear land for yourself in the territory of the Perizzites and Rephaites.

¹⁶ The descendants of Joseph replied, The hill country is not enough for us, and the Canaanites living in the valley all have iron chariots — both those in Beth Shean and its settlements and those in the Valley of Jezreel. ¹⁷ But Joshua said to the tribes of Joseph — to Ephraim and Manasseh — You are a numerous people and you have great power. You will not have just one allotment. ¹⁸ The forested hill country will be yours as well. Though it is heavily wooded, clear it and its farthest limits will be yours. Even though the Canaanites have iron chariots and are strong, you can drive them out.

[Chapter 18] ¹ The whole Israelite community assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land had been brought under their control, ² but there were still seven Israelite tribes who had not yet received their inheritance. ³ Joshua said to the Israelites, How long will you wait before taking possession of the land that the LORD God of your ancestors has given you? ⁴ Appoint three men from each tribe. I will send them out to map the land, making a record of it as it relates to each tribe's inheritance, and they will return to me. ⁵ You are to divide the land into seven portions. Judah is to remain in its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph is to remain in its territory in the north.

⁶ Survey the land and write a description of it in seven sections, then bring it back to me. I will cast lots for you here in the presence of the LORD our God. ⁷ The Levites, however, are not to have a portion among you, because the priestly service of the LORD is their inheritance. And Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them. ⁸ The men left and began their survey. Joshua instructed them, Go and walk through the land, map it out, and return to me. Then I will cast lots for you here at Shiloh before the LORD. ⁹ So they went through the land and described it town by town in a scroll, dividing it into seven sections. Then they returned to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh. ¹⁰ Joshua then cast lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD and distributed the land to the Israelites according to their tribal divisions.

¹¹ The lot for the tribe of Benjamin came up first. Their allotted territory lay between the tribes of Judah and Joseph. ¹² On the north side their boundary began at the Jordan, went up to the ridge north of Jericho, and headed westward into the hill country, ending at the wilderness of Beth Aven. ¹³ From there the boundary went south to Luz — that is, Bethel — and descended to Ataroth Addar near the hill that lies south of Lower Beth Horon. ¹⁴ The boundary then drew a line along the southern slope of the hill opposite Beth Horon and turned southward, ending at Kiriath Baal — that is, Kiriath Jearim — a town belonging to the people of Judah. This was the western side. ¹⁵ The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath Jearim, and the boundary went westward to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

¹⁶ The boundary then went down to the foot of the hill facing the Valley of Ben Hinnom, north of the Valley of Rephaim, descended into the Hinnom Valley to the southern slope of the Jebusite ridge, and went down to En Rogel. ¹⁷ It curved north, went out to En Shemesh, then to Geliloth facing the Pass of Adummim, and descended to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben. ¹⁸ It then passed along the northern slope overlooking the Arabah and went down into the Arabah. ¹⁹ The boundary continued along the northern slope of Beth Hoglah and ended at the northern bay of the Dead Sea, at the south end of the Jordan. This was the southern boundary. ²⁰ The Jordan was the eastern boundary. These were the boundaries on all sides for the clans of Benjamin's inheritance.

²¹ The towns of the tribe of Benjamin by their clans were Jericho, Beth Hoglah, the Valley of Keziz, ²² Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, ²³ Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, ²⁴ Kephar Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba — twelve towns with their villages. ²⁵ Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,

²⁶ Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah, ²⁷ Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, ²⁸ Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite city (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah, and Kiriath — fourteen towns with their villages. This is the inheritance of the tribe of Benjamin by its clans.

[Chapter 19] ¹ The second lot fell to the tribe of Simeon, for their clans. Their territory lay within the territory of Judah. ² Their allotment included Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah, ³ Hazar-shual, Balah, and Ezem, ⁴ Eltolad, Bethul, and Hormah, ⁵ Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah,

⁶ Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen — thirteen cities with their villages. ⁷ Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan — four cities with their villages. ⁸ And all the settlements around these cities as far as Baalath-beer (Ramah of the Negev). This was the inheritance of the tribe of Simeon by their clans. ⁹ The Simeonites received their portion from the territory of Judah, because Judah's share was more than they needed. So Simeon received their inheritance within Judah's territory. ¹⁰ The third lot came up for the tribe of Zebulun by their clans. The boundary of their territory reached to Sarid.

¹¹ Their border went westward to Maralah, touching Dabbesheth and the stream east of Jokneam. ¹² From Sarid it turned east toward the sunrise to the boundary of Chisloth-tabor, then continued to Daberath and up to Japhia. ¹³ From there it continued east to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, extending to Rimmon and bending toward Neah. ¹⁴ The border swung around on the north side to Hannathon, and its limit was the valley of Iphtah-el. ¹⁵ Also included were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem — twelve cities with their villages.

¹⁶ This was the inheritance of the tribe of Zebulun by their clans — these cities with their villages. ¹⁷ The fourth lot came out for the tribe of Issachar by their clans. ¹⁸ Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shunem, ¹⁹ Hapharaim, Shion, and Anaharath, ²⁰ Rabbith, Kishion, and Ebez,

²¹ Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez. ²² The boundary touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, ending at the Jordan — sixteen cities with their villages. ²³ This was the inheritance of the tribe of Issachar by their clans — the cities with their villages. ²⁴ The fifth lot came out for the tribe of Asher by their clans. ²⁵ Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph,

²⁶ Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. The boundary reached westward to Carmel and Shihor-libnath, ²⁷ then turned east toward Beth-dagon, touching Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el northward, then Beth-emek and Neiel, and extended to Cabul on the left, ²⁸ Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon. ²⁹ The border turned back toward Ramah and to the fortified city of Tyre, then curved to Hosah, ending at the sea near Achzib. ³⁰ Also Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob — twenty-two cities with their villages.

³¹ This was the inheritance of the tribe of Asher by their clans — these cities with their villages. ³² The sixth lot came out for the tribe of Naphtali by their clans. ³³ Their border ran from Heleph, from the oak at Zaanannim, through Adami-nekeb and Jabneel as far as Lakkum, ending at the Jordan. ³⁴ The boundary then turned west to Aznoth-tabor, went out from there to Hukkok, and touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrise. ³⁵ The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth,

³⁶ Adamah, Ramah, and Hazor, ³⁷ Kedesh, Edrei, En-hazor, ³⁸ Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh — nineteen cities with their villages. ³⁹ This was the inheritance of the tribe of Naphtali by their clans — the cities with their villages. ⁴⁰ The seventh lot came out for the tribe of Dan by their clans.

⁴¹ The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, and Ir-shemesh, ⁴² Shaalabbin, Aijalon, and Ithlah, ⁴³ Elon, Timnah, and Ekron, ⁴⁴ Eltekeh, Gibbethon, and Baalath, ⁴⁵ Jehud, Bene-berak, and Gath-rimmon,

⁴⁶ Me-jarkon and Rakkon, with the territory facing Joppa. ⁴⁷ But the territory of the Danites was too small for them, so the Danites marched up and attacked Leshem, captured it, put it to the sword, and took possession of it. They settled there and renamed it Dan, after their ancestor. ⁴⁸ This was the inheritance of the tribe of Dan by their clans — these cities with their villages. ⁴⁹ When they had finished dividing up the land by its boundaries, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them. ⁵⁰ In keeping with the LORD's command, they gave him the town he asked for — Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He built up the town and settled there.

⁵¹ These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the tribal families of Israel distributed by lot at Shiloh before the LORD, at the entrance to the tent of meeting. And they finished dividing up the land.

[Chapter 20] ¹ The LORD said to Joshua, ² "Tell the Israelites: 'Designate the cities of refuge that I instructed you to set apart through Moses, ³ so that anyone who kills a person accidentally and unintentionally may flee there. These cities will be a refuge from the avenger of blood. ⁴ When the fugitive flees to one of these cities, he is to stand at the entrance of the city gate and state his case before the elders of that city. They are to admit him into the city and give him a place to live among them. ⁵ If the avenger of blood comes after him, they must not hand him over, because he killed his neighbor accidentally and without prior malice.

⁶ He is to stay in that city until he has stood trial before the assembly and until the death of the high priest who is serving at that time. Then he may return home to the town he fled from.' " ⁷ So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba — that is, Hebron — in the hill country of Judah. ⁸ East of the Jordan, on the other side from Jericho, they designated Bezer in the desert plateau from the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh. ⁹ These were the cities designated for all the Israelites and for the foreigners living among them, so that anyone who killed a person accidentally could flee there and not be killed by the avenger of blood before standing trial before the assembly.

[Chapter 21] ¹ The heads of the Levite families came forward to Eleazar the priest and to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the other tribal families of Israel. ² They spoke to them at Shiloh in Canaan and said, "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given towns to live in, with the surrounding pasturelands for our livestock." ³ So the Israelites gave the Levites, out of their own inheritance, the following towns and their pasturelands, as the LORD had commanded. ⁴ The lot came out for the Kohathite clans. The descendants of Aaron the priest, who were Levites, received thirteen towns by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin. ⁵ The rest of the Kohathites received ten towns by lot from the clans of the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

⁶ The Gershonites received thirteen towns by lot from the clans of the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan. ⁷ The Merarites, by their clans, received twelve towns from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun. ⁸ So the Israelites assigned these towns and their pasturelands to the Levites by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses. ⁹ From the tribes of Judah and Simeon they assigned the following towns by name — ¹⁰ these went to the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite clans within the tribe of Levi, because the first lot fell to them.

¹¹ They gave them Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron, named for Arba the forefather of Anak) in the hill country of Judah, along with the surrounding pasturelands. ¹² But the fields and villages belonging to the city they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession. ¹³ So the descendants of Aaron the priest received Hebron (a city of refuge for the accused killer) with its pasturelands, Libnah with its pasturelands, ¹⁴ Jattir with its pasturelands, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands, ¹⁵ Holon with its pasturelands, and Debir with its pasturelands,

¹⁶ Ain with its pasturelands, Juttah with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands — nine cities from these two tribes. ¹⁷ From the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon with its pasturelands and Geba with its pasturelands, ¹⁸ Anathoth with its pasturelands and Almon with its pasturelands — four cities. ¹⁹ The total number of towns given to the priests, the descendants of Aaron, was thirteen, with their pasturelands. ²⁰ The remaining Kohathite clans of the Levites received their towns by lot from the tribe of Ephraim.

²¹ They were given Shechem (a city of refuge for the accused killer) with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer with its pasturelands, ²² Kibzaim with its pasturelands, and Beth-horon with its pasturelands — four cities. ²³ From the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh with its pasturelands, Gibbethon with its pasturelands, ²⁴ Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands — four cities. ²⁵ From the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach with its pasturelands and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands — two cities.

²⁶ The total for the remaining Kohathite clans was ten cities with their pasturelands. ²⁷ The Gershonite clans of the Levites received from the other half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan (a city of refuge for the accused killer) with its pasturelands, and Beeshterah with its pasturelands — two cities. ²⁸ From the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands, ²⁹ Jarmuth with its pasturelands, and En-gannim with its pasturelands — four cities. ³⁰ From the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pasturelands, Abdon with its pasturelands,

³¹ Helkath with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands — four cities. ³² From the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee (a city of refuge for the accused killer) with its pasturelands, Hammoth-dor with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands — three cities. ³³ The total number of towns for the Gershonite clans was thirteen, with their pasturelands. ³⁴ The remaining Levites, the Merarite clans, received from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam with its pasturelands, Kartah with its pasturelands, ³⁵ Dimnah with its pasturelands, and Nahalal with its pasturelands — four cities.

³⁶ From the tribe of Reuben: Bezer with its pasturelands, Jahaz with its pasturelands, ³⁷ Kedemoth with its pasturelands, and Mephaath with its pasturelands — four cities. ³⁸ From the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead (a city of refuge for the accused killer) with its pasturelands, Mahanaim with its pasturelands, ³⁹ Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands — four cities in all. ⁴⁰ The total number of towns allotted to the Merarite clans — the remaining Levite clans — by lot was twelve.

⁴¹ The total number of towns within Israelite territory given to the Levites was forty-eight, each with its surrounding pasturelands. ⁴² Every one of these towns had its own pasturelands around it — this was true for all of them. ⁴³ So the LORD gave Israel all the land he had sworn to give their ancestors. They took possession of it and settled there. ⁴⁴ The LORD gave them rest on every side, just as he had sworn to their ancestors. None of their enemies could stand against them; the LORD gave all their enemies into their hands. ⁴⁵ Not one word of all the good promises the LORD had made to Israel failed — every single one was fulfilled.

[Chapter 22] ¹ Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. ² He said to them, "You have carried out everything Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have obeyed me in all that I commanded you. ³ You have not abandoned your fellow Israelites all this time, right up to this day. You have faithfully kept the charge the LORD your God laid on you. ⁴ Now the LORD your God has given your fellow Israelites rest, as he promised them. So go back home to your own land — the territory that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you east of the Jordan. ⁵ But be very careful to keep the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul."

⁶ Then Joshua blessed them and sent them on their way, and they went home. ⁷ Moses had given the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh their land in Bashan, while Joshua had given the western half their land among the other tribes west of the Jordan. When Joshua sent them home with his blessing, ⁸ he said, "Go home with great wealth — large herds of livestock, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and a great deal of clothing. Share the plunder from your enemies with your fellow Israelites." ⁹ So the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the Israelites at Shiloh in Canaan and headed back to Gilead, their own land, which they had received in accordance with the LORD's command through Moses. ¹⁰ When they reached the region near the Jordan in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built a large, imposing altar there beside the Jordan.

¹¹ When the rest of the Israelites heard that the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar at the edge of Canaan, at the Jordan crossing on the Israelite side, ¹² the whole assembly of Israel gathered at Shiloh, ready to go to war against them. ¹³ But first the Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead, ¹⁴ accompanied by ten leaders — one senior leader from each of the tribes of Israel, each the head of his family clan. ¹⁵ They came to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead and said to them,

¹⁶ "This is what the whole assembly of the LORD says: 'What is this act of unfaithfulness you have committed against the God of Israel by turning away from the LORD today and building yourselves an altar in rebellion against him? ¹⁷ Was the sin at Peor not enough for us — a sin from which we have not yet cleansed ourselves, and for which a plague struck the LORD's community? ¹⁸ And now you are turning away from the LORD? If you rebel against the LORD today, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole community of Israel. ¹⁹ If your land is too unclean for you, come over to the LORD's land, where the LORD's tabernacle stands, and take a share among us. But do not rebel against the LORD or against us by building an altar separate from the altar of the LORD our God. ²⁰ When Achan son of Zerah was unfaithful in taking the devoted things, did not God's anger fall on the whole community of Israel? He was not the only one who died for his sin.'"

²¹ The Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh replied to the leaders of the Israelite clans, ²² "The Mighty One, God, the LORD — the Mighty One, God, the LORD — he knows! And let Israel know as well: if this was rebellion or unfaithfulness against the LORD, do not spare us today! ²³ If we built this altar to turn away from the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings on it, or to present fellowship offerings — may the LORD himself call us to account for it. ²⁴ No! We built it out of concern over a future situation. We feared that your descendants might one day say to ours, 'What do you have to do with the LORD, the God of Israel? ²⁵ The LORD set the Jordan as a boundary between us and you Reubenites and Gadites — you have no share in the LORD.' Your descendants might cause ours to stop fearing the LORD.

²⁶ "That is why we said, 'Let us build an altar — not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, ²⁷ but as a witness between us and you and our descendants after us, that we will worship the LORD before him with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and fellowship offerings. Then in the future your descendants cannot say to ours, "You have no share in the LORD."' ²⁸ We thought, 'If they ever say this to us or to our descendants in the future, we will answer: Look at this replica of the LORD's altar, which our ancestors built — not for burnt offerings and sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you.' ²⁹ Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away from him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, and sacrifices, separate from the altar of the LORD our God that stands before his tabernacle!" ³⁰ When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the assembly — the heads of the Israelite clans — heard what the Reubenites, Gadites, and Manassites had to say, they were satisfied.

³¹ Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, Gadites, and Manassites, "Today we know that the LORD is with us, because you have not acted unfaithfully toward the LORD in this matter. You have saved the Israelites from the LORD's judgment." ³² Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the Reubenites and Gadites in Gilead to the land of Canaan and reported back to the Israelites. ³³ The Israelites were pleased with the report and praised God. They said no more about going to war against them, about destroying the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived. ³⁴ The Reubenites and Gadites named the altar "Witness," saying, "It is a witness between us that the LORD is God."

[Chapter 23] ¹ A long time passed, and the LORD had given Israel rest from all their surrounding enemies. Joshua had grown old and was advanced in years. ² He summoned all Israel — their elders, leaders, judges, and officials — and said to them, "I am now old and well along in years. ³ You yourselves have seen everything the LORD your God has done to all these nations on your behalf. It was the LORD your God who fought for you. ⁴ I have assigned to your tribes as an inheritance all the territory of the remaining nations — and all the nations I have already destroyed — from the Jordan to the Mediterranean Sea in the west. ⁵ The LORD your God will push them back before you and drive them from your land. You will take possession of their land, just as the LORD your God promised you.

⁶ Be very strong and courageous to obey everything written in the Book of the Law of Moses. Do not deviate from it to the right or to the left. ⁷ Do not associate with these remaining nations. Do not invoke the names of their gods, take oaths by them, serve them, or bow down to them. ⁸ Instead, hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day. ⁹ The LORD has driven out great and powerful nations before you, and to this day no one has been able to stand against you. ¹⁰ One of you can chase a thousand, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as he promised.

¹¹ So be very careful to love the LORD your God. ¹² But if you turn away and ally yourselves with the survivors of these nations that remain among you — if you intermarry with them and associate with them — ¹³ then know for certain that the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations before you. Instead, they will become traps and snares for you, whips on your backs and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land the LORD your God has given you. ¹⁴ I am about to go the way of all the earth. You know with all your heart and soul that not one of all the good promises the LORD your God gave you has failed — every one has been fulfilled; not one has remained unfulfilled. ¹⁵ But just as all the good things the LORD your God promised you have come true, so he will also bring on you every disaster he threatened, until he has destroyed you from this good land he has given you.

¹⁶ When you violate the covenant of the LORD your God, which he commanded you, and go after other gods and worship them, the LORD's anger will burn against you and you will quickly vanish from this good land he has given you."

[Chapter 24] ¹ Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He summoned Israel's elders, leaders, judges, and officials, and they presented themselves before God. ² Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Long ago your ancestors — including Terah the father of Abraham and Nahor — lived beyond the Euphrates River and worshiped other gods. ³ But I took your father Abraham from the land beyond the Euphrates and led him throughout the land of Canaan, and gave him many descendants through his son Isaac. ⁴ To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave the hill country of Seir to Esau, but Jacob and his family went down to Egypt. ⁵ Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I afflicted Egypt with everything I did there, and afterward I brought you out.

⁶ When I brought your fathers out of Egypt, you came to the sea, and the Egyptians pursued them with chariots and cavalry as far as the Red Sea. ⁷ When they cried out to the LORD, he placed darkness between you and the Egyptians, brought the sea crashing down on them, and overwhelmed them. You witnessed with your own eyes what I did to Egypt. After that you lived in the wilderness for a long time. ⁸ I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived east of the Jordan. They fought against you, but I handed them over to you. You conquered their land, and I destroyed them before you. ⁹ Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, prepared to fight against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you. ¹⁰ But I refused to listen to Balaam, so he blessed you again and again. And I rescued you from his power.

¹¹ You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The citizens of Jericho fought against you, as did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites — but I handed them all over to you. ¹² I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove them out — including the two Amorite kings — not by your sword or your bow. ¹³ I gave you land you did not work for, cities you did not build, and here you live and eat from vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.' ¹⁴ "Now therefore, fear the LORD and serve him completely and faithfully. Throw away the gods your ancestors worshiped beyond the Euphrates and in Egypt, and serve the LORD. ¹⁵ But if you are unwilling to serve the LORD, then choose today whom you will serve — whether the gods your ancestors worshiped beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. As for me and my family, we will serve the LORD."

¹⁶ The people answered, "We would never abandon the LORD to serve other gods! ¹⁷ For the LORD our God brought us and our ancestors up out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. He performed those great signs before our eyes, and he protected us on our entire journey and among all the nations through which we traveled. ¹⁸ The LORD drove out from before us all the nations, including the Amorites who lived in this land. We too will serve the LORD, for he is our God." ¹⁹ Then Joshua said to the people, "You cannot serve the LORD, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God — he will not forgive your rebellion and your sins. ²⁰ If you abandon the LORD and serve foreign gods, he will turn against you and harm you and destroy you, after he has been good to you."

²¹ But the people said to Joshua, "No, we will serve the LORD." ²² And Joshua said, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen to serve the LORD." "Yes, we are witnesses," they replied. ²³ "Then put away the foreign gods that are among you," he said, "and turn your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel." ²⁴ And the people said to Joshua, "We will serve the LORD our God and obey him." ²⁵ That day Joshua made a covenant with the people at Shechem, establishing a decree and an ordinance for them.

²⁶ Joshua recorded all of this in the Book of the Law of God. Then he took a large stone and set it up there under the oak tree near the LORD's sanctuary. ²⁷ Joshua said to all the people, "This stone will be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words the LORD spoke to us. It will be a witness against you if you are ever unfaithful to your God." ²⁸ Then Joshua dismissed the people, each to their own inheritance. ²⁹ After all this, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred and ten. ³⁰ He was buried at Timnath-serah, within the boundaries of his own inheritance in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

³¹ Israel served the LORD throughout Joshua's lifetime and during the lifetimes of the elders who outlived him — those who had experienced everything the LORD had done for Israel. ³² The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem in the plot of ground that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred pieces of silver. This land became the inheritance of Joseph's descendants. ³³ And Eleazar son of Aaron died and was buried at Gibeah, which had been given to his son Phinehas in the hill country of Ephraim.

chapters.title: Judges
paragraphs: ¹ After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the LORD, "Who should go up first to fight the Canaanites for us?" ² The LORD answered, "Judah shall go up. I have given the land into their hands." ³ Then Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come with me into my allotted territory to fight the Canaanites, and I'll come with you into yours." So Simeon went with him. ⁴ Judah went up, and the LORD gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hands. They struck down ten thousand men at Bezek. ⁵ There they found Adoni-bezek and fought him, defeating the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

⁶ Adoni-bezek fled, but they chased him down, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes. ⁷ Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have picked up scraps under my table. Now God has paid me back for what I did to them." They brought him to Jerusalem, where he died. ⁸ The men of Judah had also attacked Jerusalem, captured it, put it to the sword, and set the city on fire. ⁹ After that, the men of Judah went down to fight the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev, and the lowlands. ¹⁰ Judah then marched against the Canaanites living in Hebron — formerly called Kiriath-arba — and defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

¹¹ From there they advanced against the people of Debir, formerly called Kiriath-sepher. ¹² Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever attacks and captures Kiriath-sepher." ¹³ Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife. ¹⁴ When she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb asked her, "What do you want?" ¹⁵ She replied, "Give me a gift. You've given me land in the Negev — now give me springs of water too." So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.

¹⁶ The descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenite, went up from the City of Palms with the people of Judah into the Judean wilderness near Arad, and settled among the people there. ¹⁷ Then Judah went with his brother Simeon and they struck down the Canaanites living in Zephath, completely destroying it. So the place was named Hormah. ¹⁸ Judah also took Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, each city with its surrounding territory. ¹⁹ The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country; but they could not drive out the people of the plains because those people had iron chariots. ²⁰ As Moses had promised, Hebron was given to Caleb, and he drove out the three sons of Anak from there.

²¹ But the Benjaminites failed to drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem, and to this day the Jebusites still live there among the Benjaminites. ²² The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them. ²³ When they sent scouts to Bethel — formerly called Luz — ²⁴ the scouts saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Show us how to get into the city, and we'll treat you well." ²⁵ He showed them the entrance, and they put the city to the sword, but let the man and his entire family go free.

²⁶ The man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city there, and named it Luz — which is still its name today. ²⁷ Manasseh did not drive out the people of Beth-shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, or Megiddo, along with their surrounding villages; the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land. ²⁸ When Israel grew strong enough, they put the Canaanites to forced labor but never fully drove them out. ²⁹ Nor did Ephraim drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; the Canaanites continued living among them there. ³⁰ Zebulun did not drive out the people of Kitron or Nahalol; the Canaanites remained among them but were put to forced labor.

³¹ Asher did not drive out the people of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob. ³² The Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land and never drove them out. ³³ Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth-shemesh or Beth-anath; they too lived among the Canaanite population, though the people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath were subjected to forced labor. ³⁴ The Amorites pushed the Danites back into the hill country and would not let them come down to the valley. ³⁵ The Amorites held their ground at Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim, but when the power of Joseph's house grew strong, the Amorites were put to forced labor.
³⁶ The territory of the Amorites extended from the Scorpion Pass to Sela and beyond.

[Chapter 2] ¹ The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bokim and said, "I brought you out of Egypt and led you into the land I swore to give your ancestors. I said I would never break my covenant with you, ² but you must make no agreement with the people of this land — you must tear down their altars. Yet you have disobeyed me. Why have you done this? ³ Now I tell you, I will not drive them out before you; they will become thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a trap for you." ⁴ When the angel of the LORD said these things to all the Israelites, the people wept aloud. ⁵ They named that place Bokim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD.

⁶ When Joshua had dismissed the people, the Israelites each went to take possession of their own allotted territory. ⁷ The people served the LORD throughout Joshua's lifetime and throughout the lifetimes of the elders who outlived him — those who had seen all the great things the LORD had done for Israel. ⁸ Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of a hundred and ten. ⁹ He was buried within the borders of his own inheritance at Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash. ¹⁰ After that whole generation was gone, a new generation grew up who knew nothing of the LORD or the things he had done for Israel.

¹¹ Then the Israelites did evil in the LORD's sight and served the Baals. ¹² They abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors who had brought them out of Egypt, and they followed other gods — the gods of the surrounding peoples. They bowed down to those gods and provoked the LORD to anger. ¹³ They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths. ¹⁴ The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he handed them over to raiders who plundered them. He sold them to their enemies all around, so that Israel could no longer hold its ground against them. ¹⁵ Whenever Israel went out to fight, the LORD's hand was against them for disaster, just as he had warned and sworn he would do. They were in great distress.

¹⁶ But the LORD raised up judges who rescued Israel from the hands of those who plundered them. ¹⁷ Yet the people would not listen to their judges; they chased after other gods, bowing down to them. They quickly turned from the path their ancestors had walked — the path of obedience to the LORD's commands. ¹⁸ Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for them, he was with that judge and rescued the people from their enemies as long as the judge lived — for the LORD had compassion on them as they groaned under their oppressors. ¹⁹ But when the judge died, the people returned to their corrupt ways, behaving even worse than their ancestors. They would not give up their evil practices or their stubborn ways. ²⁰ So the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he said, "Because this nation has violated the covenant I commanded their ancestors and has not listened to me,

²¹ I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died. ²² Through them I will test Israel — to see whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their ancestors did, or not." ²³ That is why the LORD left those nations in place, rather than quickly driving them out. He had not handed them over to Joshua.

[Chapter 3] ¹ These are the nations the LORD left in the land to test the Israelites — all those who had not experienced any of the wars in Canaan. ² He did this to teach warfare to the descendants of the Israelites who had not previously known battle. ³ He left the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in the Lebanon mountains from Mount Baal-hermon to the entrance of Hamath. ⁴ They were left to test Israel — to see whether they would obey the LORD's commands, which he had given their ancestors through Moses. ⁵ The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

⁶ They took the daughters of these peoples as wives and gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods. ⁷ The Israelites did evil in the LORD's sight; they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs. ⁸ The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia. The Israelites were subject to him for eight years. ⁹ When they cried out to the LORD, he raised up a deliverer for them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. ¹⁰ The Spirit of the LORD came on him, and he led Israel. When he went out to war, the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hands, and Othniel overpowered him.

¹¹ The land had peace for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died. ¹² The Israelites again did evil in the LORD's sight, and because of this the LORD gave Eglon king of Moab power over them. ¹³ Eglon gathered the Ammonites and the Amalekites, attacked Israel, and captured the City of Palms. ¹⁴ The Israelites were subject to Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years. ¹⁵ Again they cried out to the LORD, and he raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera the Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The Israelites sent tribute to Eglon king of Moab through Ehud.

¹⁶ Ehud had made himself a double-edged sword about eighteen inches long, which he strapped to his right thigh under his clothing. ¹⁷ He brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab, who was a very fat man. ¹⁸ After Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent off the men who had carried it. ¹⁹ But he himself turned back at the carved stones near Gilgal and said, "Your Majesty, I have a secret message for you." The king said, "Silence!" and all his attendants left. ²⁰ Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in his cool upper room and said, "I have a message from God for you." As the king rose from his seat,

²¹ Ehud reached with his left hand, drew the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into the king's belly. ²² The handle sank in after the blade, and the fat closed over it — he could not pull the sword out of his belly, and the contents of his bowels spilled out. ²³ Then Ehud went out through the porch, shut the doors of the upper room behind him, and locked them. ²⁴ After he had gone, the servants came back and found the doors of the upper room locked. They said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool inner room." ²⁵ They waited until they were embarrassed, but when he still did not open the doors, they took a key and unlocked them — and there was their master, fallen dead on the floor.

²⁶ While they were waiting, Ehud escaped; he slipped past the carved stones and made it safely to Seirah. ²⁷ When he arrived, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came down from the hills with him at their head. ²⁸ He told them, "Follow me! The LORD has given your enemies the Moabites into your hands." So they followed him down, seized the fords of the Jordan ahead of the Moabites, and allowed no one to cross. ²⁹ At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites — all vigorous, strong men; not one escaped. ³⁰ That day Moab was subdued under Israel's hand, and the land had peace for eighty years.
³¹ After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad. He too saved Israel.

[Chapter 4] ¹ After Ehud died, the Israelites again did evil in the LORD's sight. ² So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who ruled in Hazor. His army commander was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-haggoyim. ³ Because Jabin had nine hundred iron chariots and had cruelly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years, they cried out to the LORD for help. ⁴ Now Deborah, a prophet, the wife of Lappidoth, was leading Israel at that time. ⁵ She held court under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came to her to have their disputes settled.

⁶ She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, "Has the LORD God of Israel not commanded you: 'Go, march to Mount Tabor and take ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun with you'? ⁷ I will draw Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, with his chariots and troops, to the Kishon River, and hand him over to you." ⁸ Barak answered her, "If you go with me, I'll go; but if you don't go with me, I won't go." ⁹ "I will certainly go with you," she said, "but the road you're taking will bring you no glory, because the LORD will hand Sisera over to a woman." So Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh. ¹⁰ Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men followed him. Deborah went up with him as well.

¹¹ Now Heber the Kenite — a descendant of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law — had separated from the other Kenites and pitched his tent near the great tree at Zaanannim, near Kedesh. ¹² When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor, ¹³ he called together all nine hundred of his iron chariots and all the troops he had, marching from Harosheth-haggoyim to the Kishon River. ¹⁴ Then Deborah said to Barak, "Go! This is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hands. Has not the LORD gone ahead of you?" So Barak charged down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him. ¹⁵ The LORD threw Sisera, all his chariots, and his entire army into a panic before Barak's sword. Sisera abandoned his chariot and fled on foot.

¹⁶ Barak pursued the chariots and the army all the way to Harosheth-haggoyim. The whole army of Sisera fell by the sword; not one man was left. ¹⁷ But Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, because Jabin king of Hazor and the family of Heber the Kenite were at peace. ¹⁸ Jael came out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Come in, my lord, come right in. Don't be afraid." So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a blanket. ¹⁹ He said to her, "Please give me some water. I'm thirsty." She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him up again. ²⁰ "Stand at the entrance to the tent," he told her. "If anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there anyone here?' say no."

²¹ But Jael, Heber's wife, picked up a tent peg and a hammer. While Sisera lay sleeping from exhaustion, she drove the peg through his temple and into the ground, and he died. ²² Just then Barak came by in pursuit of Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. "Come," she said, "I'll show you the man you're looking for." He went in with her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the tent peg through his temple. ²³ So on that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites. ²⁴ And the power of Israel grew stronger and stronger against Jabin king of Canaan until they finally destroyed him.

[Chapter 5] ¹ On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song: ² "When the princes of Israel take the lead, when the people willingly offer themselves — praise the LORD! ³ Hear this, you kings! Listen, you rulers! I, yes I, will sing to the LORD; I will praise the LORD God of Israel. ⁴ LORD, when you marched out from Seir, when you strode forth from the land of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens poured, the clouds poured down water. ⁵ The mountains melted before the LORD, even Sinai before the LORD, the God of Israel.

⁶ In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the main roads were abandoned; travelers kept to back roads. ⁷ Village life in Israel had ceased, ceased until I, Deborah, arose — arose as a mother in Israel. ⁸ When they chose new gods, war came to the city gates. Not a shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel. ⁹ My heart is with Israel's commanders, with the willing volunteers among the people. Praise the LORD! ¹⁰ You who ride white donkeys, who sit on fine saddle blankets, who walk along the road — sing out!

¹¹ Listen to the voices of the singers at the watering places — there they recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous acts of his warriors in Israel. Then the LORD's people marched down to the city gates. ¹² Wake up, wake up, Deborah! Wake up, wake up, break into song! Rise up, Barak! Take captive your captives, son of Abinoam. ¹³ Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the LORD's people came down to me against the mighty. ¹⁴ Some came from Ephraim, whose roots were in Amalek; Benjamin followed with your people. From Makir, commanders marched down; from Zebulun, those who carry the commander's staff. ¹⁵ The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; yes, Issachar was with Barak, rushing after him into the valley. In the regions of Reuben there was much searching of heart.

¹⁶ Why did you stay among the sheep pens listening to the pipes for the flocks? In the regions of Reuben there was much searching of heart. ¹⁷ Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan. And why did Dan remain in ships? ²¹ The LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and his whole army into Israel's hand. Israel defeated them and took possession of all the land of the Amorites who lived in that country. ²² They took over all the Amorite territory from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan. ²³ Since the LORD, the God of Israel, drove out the Amorites before his people Israel, what right do you have to take it over? ²⁴ Take whatever your god Chemosh gives you, and we will take whatever the LORD our God gives us! ²⁵ Are you any better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel or go to war against them?

²⁶ Israel has been living in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the towns along the Arnon for three hundred years. Why haven't you reclaimed them during all that time? ²⁷ I have not wronged you, but you are doing wrong by making war against me. Let the LORD, the Judge, decide the dispute this day between the Israelites and the Ammonites." But the king of the Ammonites ignored Jephthah's message. ²⁹ Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah. He passed through Gilead and Manasseh, through Mizpah in Gilead, and from there crossed over to the Ammonites. ³⁰ And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD: "If you give the Ammonites into my hands,

³¹ then whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return triumphant from the Ammonites will be the LORD's, and I will sacrifice it as a burnt offering." ³² So Jephthah crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into his hands. ³³ He devastated twenty towns from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith and all the way to Abel-keramim. Thus Israel subdued Ammon. ³⁴ When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, his daughter came out to meet him, dancing to the sound of tambourines! She was his only child — he had no son or daughter besides her. ³⁵ When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, "Oh no, my daughter! You have brought me to my knees! You are one of those who trouble me — for I have given my word to the LORD and I cannot take it back."

³⁶ She replied, "My father, you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me as you promised, now that the LORD has vindicated you against your enemies, the Ammonites." ³⁷ She added, "Grant me this one request. Give me two months to roam the hills and weep with my friends, because I will never marry." ³⁸ "Go," he said. And he let her go for two months. She and her companions went into the hills and wept for her lost future. ³⁹ At the end of two months she returned to her father, and he kept the vow he had made. She had never been with a man. This gave rise to a custom in Israel: ⁴⁰ each year the young women of Israel would go out for four days to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.

[Chapter 12] ¹ The men of Ephraim mustered their forces and crossed north to Zaphon. They said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We're going to burn your house down over you!" ² Jephthah answered them, "I and my people were in a great struggle with the Ammonites, and when I called you, you didn't save me from their hands. ³ When I saw that you weren't going to help, I took my life in my hands and crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them to me. Why are you coming to fight me today?" ⁴ Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. The Gileadites struck Ephraim down — for the Ephraimites had said, "You Gileadites are renegades from Ephraim and Manasseh!" ⁵ The Gileadites captured the fords of the Jordan before Ephraim could get there. Whenever a survivor of Ephraim said, "Let me cross," the men of Gilead would ask, "Are you an Ephraimite?" If he said no,

⁶ they would say, "Then say 'Shibboleth.'" If he said "Sibboleth," because he could not pronounce the word correctly, they would seize him and kill him at the ford of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand Ephraimites were killed at that time. ⁷ Jephthah led Israel for six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the towns of Gilead. ⁸ After him, Ibzan of Bethlehem became judge over Israel. ⁹ He had thirty sons and thirty daughters. He arranged marriages for all his daughters outside his clan and brought in thirty young women from outside his clan for his sons. He led Israel for seven years. ¹⁰ Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.

¹¹ After him, Elon the Zebulunite became judge over Israel and led it for ten years. ¹² Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun. ¹³ After him, Abdon the son of Hillel, from Pirathon, became judge over Israel. ¹⁴ He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He led Israel for eight years. ¹⁵ Then Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

[Chapter 13] ¹ Again the Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD handed them over to the Philistines for forty years. ² A certain man of Zorah, from the tribe of Dan, whose name was Manoah, had a wife who was barren and had borne no children. ³ The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "You are barren and childless, but you are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son. ⁴ Now then, be careful not to drink wine or other fermented drink and not to eat anything unclean. ⁵ You will become pregnant and have a son whose head is never to be touched by a razor, because the boy will be dedicated to God as a Nazirite from the womb. He will begin the deliverance of Israel from the Philistines."

⁶ Then the woman went and told her husband: "A man of God came to me. He looked like an angel of God — very awe-inspiring. I didn't ask him where he came from, and he didn't tell me his name. ⁷ But he said to me, 'You are going to become pregnant and give birth to a son. Don't drink wine or other fermented drink and don't eat anything unclean, because the boy will be dedicated to God as a Nazirite from birth until the day of his death.'" ⁸ Then Manoah prayed to the LORD: "Please, Lord, let the man of God you sent come to us again to teach us how to raise the boy who is to be born." ⁹ God heard Manoah's prayer, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field. But her husband Manoah was not with her. ¹⁰ The woman hurried to tell her husband, "The man who appeared to me the other day is here!"

¹¹ Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he asked, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife?" "I am," he said. ¹² Manoah asked, "When your word comes true, what will be the rules for the boy's life and work?" ¹³ The angel of the LORD replied, "Let the woman pay attention to everything I told her. ¹⁴ She must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, nor drink wine or other fermented drink, nor eat anything unclean. She must do everything I commanded her." ¹⁵ Then Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "Please stay and let us prepare a young goat for you."

¹⁶ The angel of the LORD replied, "Even if you keep me here, I will not eat your food. But if you want to prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." For Manoah did not yet realize that it was the angel of the LORD. ¹⁷ Then Manoah asked the angel of the LORD, "What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes true?" ¹⁸ The angel of the LORD replied, "Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding." ¹⁹ Then Manoah took a young goat and a grain offering and sacrificed them on a rock to the LORD. And the LORD did something remarkable while Manoah and his wife watched. ²⁰ As the flame blazed up from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame. Seeing this, Manoah and his wife fell face down on the ground.

²¹ The angel of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah realized it was the angel of the LORD. ²² "We are going to die!" he said to his wife. "We have seen God!" ²³ But his wife replied, "If the LORD had meant to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and grain offering from our hands, nor shown us all these things, nor told us this at this time." ²⁴ The woman gave birth to a boy and named him Samson. The child grew and the LORD blessed him. ²⁵ The Spirit of the LORD began to stir him while he was in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

[Chapter 14] ¹ Samson went down to Timnah and saw a young Philistine woman there. ² When he returned home, he told his father and mother, "I've seen a Philistine woman in Timnah. Get her for me as my wife." ³ His father and mother replied, "Isn't there an acceptable woman among the women of your relatives or among all our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?" But Samson said to his father, "Get her for me. She's the right one for me." ⁴ His parents did not know that this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion to confront the Philistines. At that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel. ⁵ Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. As they approached the vineyards of Timnah, suddenly a young lion came roaring toward him.

⁶ The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon Samson, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as he might have torn a young goat — yet he told neither his father nor his mother what he had done. ⁷ Then he went down and talked with the woman, and he liked her. ⁸ Some time later, when he went back to marry her, he turned aside to look at the lion's carcass, and he saw a swarm of bees and some honey there. ⁹ He scooped it out with his hands and ate it as he walked along. He gave some to his parents, and they also ate it. But he didn't tell them he had taken the honey from the lion's carcass. ¹⁰ Then his father went down to see the woman. Samson held a feast there, as was the custom for young men.

¹¹ When the Philistines saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him. ¹² Samson said to them, "Let me tell you a riddle. If you can give me the answer within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes. ¹³ But if you can't tell me the answer, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes." "Tell us your riddle," they said. "Let's hear it." ¹⁴ He said to them, "Out of the eater, something to eat; out of the strong, something sweet." For three days they could not solve the riddle. ¹⁵ On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband into explaining the riddle for us, or we will burn you and your father's household. Did you invite us here to rob us?"

¹⁶ Samson's wife threw herself on him, sobbing, "You hate me! You don't really love me. You've given my people a riddle but you haven't told me the answer." On the seventh day he finally told her, because she had pressed him so hard. She then told the riddle's answer to her people. ¹⁸ Before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the town said to Samson, "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" Samson answered, "If you hadn't plowed with my heifer, you wouldn't have solved my riddle!" ¹⁹ Then the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him. He went down to Ashkelon, struck down thirty of their men, stripped them of their belongings, and gave their clothes to those who had answered the riddle. Burning with anger, he went up to his father's house. ²⁰ And Samson's wife was given to the companion who had attended him at the feast.

[Chapter 15] ¹ Later on, during the wheat harvest, Samson went to visit his wife, bringing a young goat as a gift. He said, "I want to go to my wife in her room."
