⁶ Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah, ⁷ Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah. These were the leaders of the priests and their associates in the days of Jeshua. ⁸ The Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah — who, together with his associates, was in charge of the songs of thanksgiving. ⁹ Bakbukiah and Unni, their associates, stood opposite them in the services. ¹⁰ Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim the father of Eliashib, Eliashib the father of Joiada,

¹¹ Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua. ¹² In the days of Joiakim, these were the heads of the priestly families: of Seraiah's family, Meraiah; of Jeremiah's, Hananiah; ¹³ of Ezra's, Meshullam; of Amariah's, Jehohanan; ¹⁴ of Malluch's, Jonathan; of Shebaniah's, Joseph; ¹⁵ of Harim's, Adna; of Meremoth's, Helkai.

¹⁶ of Iddo's family, Zechariah; of Ginnethon's, Meshullam; ¹⁷ of Abijah's, Zichri; of Miniamin's and of Moadiah's, Piltai; ¹⁸ of Bilgah's, Shammua; of Shemaiah's, Jehonathan; ¹⁹ of Joiarib's, Mattenai; of Jedaiah's, Uzzi; ²⁰ of Sallai's, Kallai; of Amok's, Eber.

²¹ of Hilkiah's family, Hashabiah; of Jedaiah's, Nethaneel. ²² The Levites were recorded as heads of families in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, as were the priests, up to the reign of Darius the Persian. ²³ The descendants of Levi who were heads of families were recorded in the book of the annals up to the time of Johanan son of Eliashib. ²⁴ And the leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Kadmiel son of Jeshua. Their associates stood opposite them to give praise and thanksgiving, one section responding to the other, as prescribed by David the man of God. ²⁵ Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.

²⁶ These were in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest and teacher of the Law. ²⁷ At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, the Levites were sought out from where they lived and were brought to Jerusalem to celebrate joyfully the dedication with songs of thanksgiving and with the music of cymbals, harps, and lyres. ²⁸ The musicians also were brought together from the region around Jerusalem — from the villages of the Netophathites, ²⁹ from Beth-Gilgal, and from the area of Geba and Azmaveth, for the musicians had built villages for themselves around Jerusalem. ³⁰ When the priests and Levites had purified themselves ceremonially, they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.

³¹ I had the leaders of Judah go up on top of the wall. I also assigned two large choirs to give thanks. One proceeded to the right on top of the wall toward the Dung Gate. ³² Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah followed them, ³³ along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, ³⁴ Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah, ³⁵ as well as some priests with trumpets, and also Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,

³⁶ and his associates — Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethaneel, Judah, and Hanani — with musical instruments prescribed by David the man of God. Ezra the teacher of the Law led the procession. ³⁷ At the Fountain Gate they continued directly up the steps of the City of David on the ascent to the wall and passed above the house of David to the Water Gate on the east. ³⁸ The second choir proceeded in the opposite direction. I followed them on top of the wall, together with half the people — past the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall, ³⁹ over the Gate of Ephraim, the Jeshanah Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. At the Gate of the Guard they stopped. ⁴⁰ The two choirs that gave thanks then took their places in the house of God; so did I, together with half the officials,

⁴¹ as well as the priests — Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah with their trumpets — ⁴² and also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malkijah, Elam, and Ezer. The choirs sang under the direction of Jezrahiah. ⁴³ And on that day they offered great sacrifices, rejoicing because God had given them great joy. The women and children also rejoiced. The sound of rejoicing in Jerusalem could be heard far away. ⁴⁴ At that time men were appointed to be in charge of the storerooms for the contributions, firstfruits, and tithes. From the fields outside the towns they were to bring into the storerooms the portions required by the Law for the priests and the Levites, for Judah was pleased with the ministering priests and Levites. ⁴⁵ They performed the service of their God and the service of purification, as did also the musicians and the gatekeepers, according to the commands of David and his son Solomon.

⁴⁶ For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there had been directors for the musicians and for the songs of praise and thanksgiving to God. ⁴⁷ So in the days of Zerubbabel and of Nehemiah, all Israel contributed the daily portions for the musicians and the gatekeepers. They also set aside the portion for the other Levites, and the Levites set aside the portion for the descendants of Aaron.

¹ On that day the Book of Moses was read aloud in the hearing of the people, and there it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever be admitted into the assembly of God, ² because they had not met the Israelites with food and water but had hired Balaam to call a curse down on them. (Our God, however, turned the curse into a blessing.) ³ When the people heard this law, they excluded all who were of foreign descent from Israel. ⁴ Before this, Eliashib the priest had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God. He was closely associated with Tobiah, ⁵ and he had provided him with a large room formerly used to store the grain offerings and incense and temple articles, and also the tithes of grain, new wine, and olive oil prescribed for the Levites, musicians, and gatekeepers, as well as the contributions for the priests.

⁶ But while all this was happening, I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had returned to the king. Some time later I asked his permission ⁷ and came back to Jerusalem. Here I learned about the evil thing Eliashib had done in providing Tobiah a room in the courts of the house of God. ⁸ I was greatly displeased and threw all Tobiah's household goods out of the room. ⁹ I gave orders to purify the rooms, and then I put back into them the equipment of the house of God, with the grain offerings and the incense. ¹⁰ I also learned that the portions assigned to the Levites had not been given to them, and that all the Levites and musicians responsible for the service had gone back to their own fields.

¹¹ So I rebuked the officials and asked, "Why is the house of God neglected?" Then I called them together and stationed them at their posts. ¹² All Judah then brought the tithes of grain, new wine, and olive oil into the storerooms. ¹³ I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and a Levite named Pedaiah in charge of the storerooms, and made Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, their assistant, because they were considered trustworthy. They were responsible for distributing the supplies to their fellow Levites. ¹⁴ Remember me for this, my God, and do not blot out what I have so faithfully done for the house of my God and its services. ¹⁵ In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing in grain and loading it on donkeys, together with wine, grapes, figs, and all other kinds of loads. And they were bringing all this into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. Therefore I warned them against selling food on that day.

¹⁶ Men from Tyre who lived in Jerusalem were bringing in fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah. ¹⁷ I rebuked the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this wicked thing you are doing — desecrating the Sabbath day? ¹⁸ Didn't your ancestors do the same things, so that our God brought all this calamity on us and on this city? Now you are stirring up more wrath against Israel by desecrating the Sabbath." ¹⁹ When evening shadows fell on the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered the doors to be shut and not opened until the Sabbath was over. I stationed some of my own men at the gates so that no load could be brought in on the Sabbath day. ²⁰ Once or twice the merchants and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.

²¹ But I warned them and said, "Why do you spend the night by the wall? If you do this again, I will arrest you." From that time on they no longer came on the Sabbath. ²² Then I commanded the Levites to purify themselves and go and guard the gates in order to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this also, my God, and show mercy to me according to your great love. ²³ Moreover, in those days I saw men of Judah who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. ²⁴ Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or the language of one of the other peoples, and did not know how to speak the language of Judah. ²⁵ I rebuked them and called curses down on them. I beat some of the men and pulled out their hair. I made them take an oath in God's name and said: "You are not to give your daughters in marriage to their sons, nor are you to take their daughters in marriage for your sons or for yourselves."

²⁶ "Was it not because of marriages like these that Solomon king of Israel sinned? Among the many nations there was no king like him. He was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel, but even he was led into sin by foreign women. ²⁷ Must we hear now that you too are doing all this terrible wickedness and are being unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?" ²⁸ One of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite. And I drove him away from me. ²⁹ Remember them, my God, because they defiled the priestly office and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites. ³⁰ So I purified the priests and the Levites of everything foreign, and assigned them duties, each to his own task.
³¹ I also made provision for contributions of wood at designated times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me with favor, my God.

chapters.title: Esther
paragraphs: ¹ In the days of Ahasuerus — the Ahasuerus who ruled over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces stretching from India to Ethiopia — ² when he was sitting on his royal throne in Shushan the palace, ³ in the third year of his reign, he gave a banquet for all his officials and servants. The military commanders of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the governors of the provinces were all in attendance. ⁴ For a full hundred and eighty days he put on a display of his kingdom's glorious wealth and his own magnificent splendor. ⁵ When those days were over, the king held another feast for all the people present in Shushan the palace, great and small alike — a seven-day celebration in the courtyard of the palace garden.

⁶ The courtyard was hung with white and blue linen curtains, fastened by cords of fine linen and purple thread to silver rings on marble pillars. The couches were of gold and silver, set on a mosaic floor of red and blue and white and black marble. ⁷ Wine was served in golden cups, each one different from the next, and the royal wine flowed freely — as befitted the king's generosity. ⁸ The drinking was without restriction; the king had instructed every palace steward to let each guest do as he wished. ⁹ Meanwhile, Queen Vashti gave her own banquet for the women inside the royal palace. ¹⁰ On the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine, he commanded his seven eunuchs — Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas — who attended him personally,

¹¹ to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing her royal crown, so that the people and officials could admire her beauty, for she was lovely to look at. ¹² But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command, delivered through his eunuchs. The king was furious, and his anger blazed within him. ¹³ He consulted the wise men who understood the law — for it was his custom to seek the opinion of those versed in law and justice. ¹⁴ His closest advisors were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media who had direct access to the king and held the highest positions in the kingdom. ¹⁵ He asked them, "What does the law say we should do to Queen Vashti, since she has not obeyed the command of King Ahasuerus delivered through his eunuchs?"

¹⁶ Memucan answered before the king and the princes, "Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king but also every official and every people in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus. ¹⁷ The story of what the queen has done will spread to all the women and encourage them to despise their husbands. They will say, 'King Ahasuerus commanded Queen Vashti to be brought before him, and she refused!' ¹⁸ And this very day the noblewomen of Persia and Media who hear what the queen has done will repeat it to all the king's officials, and there will be no end of disrespect and resentment. ¹⁹ If it pleases the king, let a royal decree go out from him — and let it be recorded in the laws of the Persians and Medes so that it cannot be repealed — that Vashti is never again to appear before King Ahasuerus, and that the king should give her royal position to someone more worthy. ²⁰ When the king's decree is proclaimed throughout his vast empire, every wife will honor her husband, from the greatest to the least."

²¹ This advice pleased the king and his officials, and the king acted on Memucan's proposal. ²² He sent letters to all his royal provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in their own language, declaring that every man should be master in his own home, and that this should be announced in each people's tongue.

¹ Sometime later, when King Ahasuerus had calmed down, he thought about Vashti — what she had done and what had been decreed against her. ² His personal attendants suggested, "Let a search be made for beautiful young virgins for the king. ³ Let the king appoint commissioners in every province of his kingdom to bring all these beautiful young women to the harem in Shushan the palace, under the care of Hegai the king's eunuch, who is in charge of the women. Let them be given their beauty treatments. ⁴ Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in Vashti's place." The king liked this idea and acted on it. ⁵ Now there was in Shushan the palace a Jew named Mordecai, the son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjamite,

⁶ who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem along with the captives taken with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported. ⁷ Mordecai had raised his cousin Hadassah — that is, Esther — because she had no father or mother. The girl was lovely and beautiful, and when her parents died, Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter. ⁸ When the king's decree was proclaimed and many young women were brought to Shushan the palace under Hegai's care, Esther was among those brought to the palace. ⁹ Hegai was pleased with her and showed her favor, quickly providing her with her beauty treatments and her special food, along with seven maids chosen from the palace, and moving her and her maids into the best rooms in the harem. ¹⁰ Esther had not revealed her nationality or family background, because Mordecai had instructed her to keep it secret.

¹¹ Every day Mordecai walked back and forth near the courtyard of the harem to learn how Esther was faring and what was happening to her. ¹² Before a young woman's turn came to go in to King Ahasuerus, she had to complete twelve months of beauty treatments — six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and cosmetics, as was the custom. ¹³ When a girl's turn came, she could take with her whatever she wanted from the harem to the king's palace. ¹⁴ She would go in the evening, and the next morning she would return to a second harem under the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch who kept the concubines. She would not see the king again unless he was particularly pleased with her and summoned her by name. ¹⁵ When it was Esther's turn — the daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai who had adopted her — she asked for nothing beyond what Hegai the king's eunuch advised. And everyone who saw her was captivated by her.

¹⁶ Esther was brought to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace in the tenth month — the month of Tebeth — in the seventh year of his reign. ¹⁷ The king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she won his grace and favor more than any of the other virgins. He placed the royal crown on her head and made her queen in Vashti's place. ¹⁸ The king gave a great banquet in Esther's honor — Esther's feast — for all his officials and servants, and he proclaimed a public holiday throughout the provinces and distributed gifts with royal generosity. ¹⁹ When the virgins were assembled a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate. ²⁰ Esther still had not revealed her family background or nationality, just as Mordecai had instructed her — she continued to follow his directions as she had when he was bringing her up.

²¹ During this time, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, two of the king's eunuchs — Bigthan and Teresh, who guarded the doorway — became furious and plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus. ²² But Mordecai learned of the plot and reported it to Queen Esther, who told the king in Mordecai's name. ²³ When the matter was investigated and confirmed, both men were hanged on a gallows. All of this was recorded in the book of the chronicles in the king's presence.

¹ Some time later, King Ahasuerus honored Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, elevating him and giving him a seat of honor above all the other officials. ² All the royal officials at the king's gate would kneel down and bow to Haman, for the king had commanded this — but Mordecai refused to kneel or bow. ³ The other royal officials at the gate asked him, "Why do you disobey the king's command?" ⁴ Day after day they spoke to him, but he refused to listen, so they reported it to Haman to see whether Mordecai would get away with it — since he had told them he was a Jew. ⁵ When Haman saw for himself that Mordecai would not kneel or bow to him, he was filled with rage.

⁶ But killing Mordecai alone was not enough for him — he had learned what people Mordecai belonged to, and he decided to destroy all the Jews throughout the entire kingdom of Ahasuerus. ⁷ In the first month, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur — that is, the lot — before Haman, day after day and month after month, and it fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar. ⁸ Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a certain people scattered throughout the provinces of your kingdom who keep themselves separate. Their customs are different from those of every other people, and they do not obey the king's laws. It is not in the king's interest to tolerate them. ⁹ If it pleases the king, let a decree be issued to destroy them. I will deposit ten thousand talents of silver into the royal treasury to pay the men who carry out this business." ¹⁰ The king took his signet ring from his finger and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.

¹¹ "Keep the money," the king told Haman, "and do what you want with these people." ¹² On the thirteenth day of the first month, the royal scribes were summoned and wrote out in Haman's exact words the order to the king's satraps, governors, and officials throughout every province — each province in its own script, each people in their own language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with his signet ring. ¹³ Couriers carried the dispatches to every corner of the empire, ordering all people to destroy, kill, and annihilate all Jews — young and old, women and children — on a single day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their goods. ¹⁴ A copy of the edict was to be issued as law in every province and posted publicly so all the people could be ready for that day. ¹⁵ The couriers raced out under the king's orders, and the decree was also posted in Shushan the palace. The king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Shushan was thrown into confusion.

¹ When Mordecai learned of everything that had happened, he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes. He went through the city, crying out loudly and bitterly. ² He came as far as the king's gate, but could go no further, since no one was allowed to enter the king's gate wearing sackcloth. ³ In every province, wherever the king's command and decree reached, there was great mourning among the Jews — fasting, weeping, and wailing — and many lay in sackcloth and ashes. ⁴ When Esther's maids and eunuchs told her what was happening, she was deeply distressed. She sent clothes for Mordecai to put on so he could take off his sackcloth, but he refused them. ⁵ Then Esther summoned Hatach, one of the king's eunuchs assigned to attend her, and instructed him to go to Mordecai and find out what was wrong and why.

⁶ So Hatach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate. ⁷ Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, including the exact amount of money Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury to buy the destruction of the Jews. ⁸ He also gave him a copy of the written decree that had been issued in Shushan authorizing their annihilation, so that Hatach could show it to Esther and explain it to her. Mordecai charged him to urge Esther to go into the king's presence to plead for mercy and intercede for her people. ⁹ Hatach returned and told Esther exactly what Mordecai had said. ¹⁰ Then Esther spoke to Hatach again and gave him a message for Mordecai:

¹¹ "All the king's servants and the people of his provinces know that there is a single law for anyone — man or woman — who comes to the king in the inner court without being summoned: they are put to death. The only exception is if the king extends his golden scepter, which means they may live. And I have not been summoned to come to the king for thirty days." ¹² When Mordecai was told what Esther had said, ¹³ he sent back this reply: "Don't think for a moment that you will escape in the palace any more than all the other Jews. ¹⁴ If you stay silent at a time like this, relief and deliverance for the Jews will come from somewhere else — but you and your father's family will be destroyed. And who knows? Perhaps you have been brought to your royal position for such a time as this." ¹⁵ Then Esther sent this answer back to Mordecai:

¹⁶ "Go and gather all the Jews in Shushan and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. My maids and I will fast as well. After that, I will go to the king, even though it is against the law — and if I die, I die." ¹⁷ So Mordecai went and did everything Esther had instructed him to do.

¹ On the third day Esther dressed in her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the palace, facing the king's hall. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the throne room, facing the entrance. ² When he saw Queen Esther standing in the court, he was pleased with her and held out to her the golden scepter that was in his hand. Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter. ³ "What is it, Queen Esther?" the king asked. "What is your request? I will give you up to half the kingdom." ⁴ "If it pleases the king," Esther replied, "let the king and Haman come today to a banquet I have prepared for him." ⁵ The king said, "Bring Haman quickly so that we can do what Esther has asked." So the king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared.

⁶ As they were drinking wine, the king asked Esther, "Now — what is your petition? It will be granted. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be done." ⁷ Esther replied, "My petition and my request — ⁸ if I have found favor in the king's sight and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request — is this: let the king and Haman come to the banquet I will prepare for them tomorrow, and then I will answer the king's question." ⁹ Haman went out that day in high spirits and in excellent humor. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate and noticed that Mordecai neither stood up nor moved for him, he was filled with rage at Mordecai. ¹⁰ Nevertheless, Haman restrained himself and went home. He summoned his friends and his wife Zeresh,

¹¹ and boasted to them about his vast wealth, his many sons, how the king had honored him and elevated him above all the other officials and nobles. ¹² "What's more," Haman added, "Queen Esther invited no one but me to come with the king to the banquet she had prepared — and tomorrow I am invited to join the king again. ¹³ But none of this means anything to me as long as I keep seeing that Jew Mordecai sitting at the king's gate." ¹⁴ His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a gallows built, seventy-five feet high, and in the morning ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go to the banquet with the king in good spirits." Haman loved this idea, and he had the gallows built.

¹ That night the king could not sleep. He ordered the book of records — the chronicles — to be brought and read aloud to him. ² It was found recorded that Mordecai had exposed the plot of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the doorway, who had plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus. ³ "What honor and recognition has Mordecai received for this?" the king asked. His attendants answered, "Nothing has been done for him." ⁴ The king asked, "Who is in the court?" Haman had just arrived in the outer court of the palace to speak to the king about having Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built for him. ⁵ The attendants replied, "Haman is standing in the court." "Bring him in," the king said.

⁶ So Haman entered, and the king asked him, "What should be done for a man the king wishes to honor?" Now Haman thought to himself, "Who would the king want to honor more than me?" ⁷ So Haman answered, "For a man the king wishes to honor, ⁸ have them bring a royal robe the king himself has worn and a horse the king has ridden, one with a royal crest placed on its head. ⁹ Let the robe and horse be given to one of the king's most noble princes. Let him robe the man and lead him through the city square on the horse, proclaiming before him, 'This is what is done for the man the king wishes to honor!'" ¹⁰ "Excellent!" the king said to Haman. "Hurry — take the robe and the horse just as you have said, and do exactly this for Mordecai the Jew who sits at the king's gate. Do not leave out a single detail."

¹¹ So Haman took the robe and the horse, dressed Mordecai, and led him through the city square on horseback, proclaiming before him, "This is what is done for the man the king wishes to honor!" ¹² Afterward Mordecai returned to the king's gate. But Haman rushed home in a panic, his head covered in shame. ¹³ Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him. His wise men and his wife Zeresh said to him, "If Mordecai — before whom your downfall has begun — is of Jewish descent, you cannot prevail against him. You will only continue to fall before him." ¹⁴ They were still talking with him when the king's eunuchs arrived and hurried Haman away to the banquet Esther had prepared.

¹ So the king and Haman went to dine with Queen Esther. ² On this second day, as they were drinking wine, the king again asked Esther, "What is your petition, Queen Esther? It will be granted. What is your request? Even up to half the kingdom, it will be done." ³ Then Queen Esther answered, "If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be spared at my petition, and my people at my request. ⁴ For my people and I have been sold to be destroyed, killed, and annihilated. If we had merely been sold as male and female slaves, I would have stayed quiet, since that trouble would not have been worth troubling the king." ⁵ King Ahasuerus asked Queen Esther, "Who is he? Where is the man who has dared to do such a thing?"

⁶ Esther said, "The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman." Haman was terrified before the king and queen. ⁷ The king got up in a rage and went into the palace garden, while Haman stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life, because he could see that the king had already decided to destroy him. ⁸ When the king returned from the palace garden to the banqueting hall, Haman had thrown himself onto the couch where Esther was reclining. "Will he even assault the queen right here in my own palace?" the king burst out. The moment those words left his mouth, the servants covered Haman's face. ⁹ Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said, "A gallows seventy-five feet high is standing at Haman's house — the very one Haman had built for Mordecai, who spoke up to help the king." "Hang him on it!" the king commanded. ¹⁰ So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had built for Mordecai, and the king's fury subsided.

¹ That same day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai came before the king, because Esther had revealed how he was related to her. ² The king removed his signet ring — which he had reclaimed from Haman — and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's estate. ³ Esther again pleaded with the king, falling at his feet and weeping, begging him to stop the evil plan of Haman the Agagite and the scheme he had plotted against the Jews. ⁴ The king held out the golden scepter to Esther, and she rose and stood before him. ⁵ "If it pleases the king," she said, "and if I have found favor in his sight — if the king thinks it right and I am pleasing to him — let an order be written to revoke the letters that Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite devised, ordering the destruction of all the Jews in every province of the king.

⁶ For how can I bear to see disaster fall on my people? How can I bear to watch the destruction of my own family?" ⁷ King Ahasuerus replied to Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, "I have already given Esther the estate of Haman, and he has been hanged on the gallows because he plotted against the Jews. ⁸ Now write a new decree in the king's name on behalf of the Jews as it seems best to you, and seal it with the king's signet ring — for a decree written in the king's name and sealed with his ring cannot be revoked." ⁹ The royal secretaries were summoned immediately — on the twenty-third day of the third month, the month of Sivan. They wrote out all of Mordecai's orders to the Jews, to the satraps, governors, and officials of the hundred and twenty-seven provinces stretching from India to Ethiopia, to each province in its own script and each people in their own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language. ¹⁰ He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed the orders with the king's signet ring, and sent them by mounted couriers riding royal horses bred from the royal stud:

¹¹ The king's decree granted the Jews in every city the right to assemble and defend themselves — to destroy, kill, and annihilate any armed force of any nationality or province that might attack them or their women and children, and to plunder the property of their enemies. ¹² This was to be done in a single day throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus — on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar. ¹³ A copy of the text of this edict was to be issued as law in every province and published to all peoples, so that the Jews would be ready to avenge themselves on their enemies on that day. ¹⁴ The couriers, riding the royal horses, rode out in haste under the king's urgent command, and the edict was also issued in Shushan the palace. ¹⁵ Mordecai left the palace wearing royal garments of blue and white, a large crown of gold, and a robe of fine linen and purple. The city of Shushan burst into joyful celebration.

¹⁶ For the Jews, it was a time of light and gladness, of joy and honor. ¹⁷ In every province and every city where the king's command and decree arrived, the Jews celebrated with joy and feasting, and declared it a holiday. And many people of other nationalities converted to Judaism, because fear of the Jews had seized them.

¹ On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month — the month of Adar — when the king's command and decree were about to be carried out, the very day on which the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, everything turned around: the Jews overpowered those who hated them. ² Throughout every province of King Ahasuerus, the Jews gathered in their cities to attack whoever sought to harm them. No one could stand against them, because all the peoples were afraid of them. ³ All the provincial officials, the satraps, the governors, and the king's administrators helped the Jews, because fear of Mordecai had fallen on them. ⁴ Mordecai had become powerful in the king's palace, and his fame was spreading throughout all the provinces — for he was becoming greater and greater. ⁵ The Jews struck down all their enemies with swords, killing and destroying them, doing as they wished to those who hated them.

⁶ In Shushan the palace, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men. ⁷ They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, and Aspatha, ⁸ Poratha, Adalia, and Aridatha, ⁹ Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vajezatha — ¹⁰ the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

¹¹ That same day the number of those killed in Shushan the palace was reported to the king. ¹² The king said to Queen Esther, "The Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, including Haman's ten sons. What must they have done in the rest of my provinces! Now what is your further petition? It will be granted. What more do you request? It shall be done." ¹³ Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, give the Jews in Shushan permission to do tomorrow what they did today, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows." ¹⁴ The king commanded this to be done, and the decree was issued in Shushan. Haman's ten sons were hanged. ¹⁵ The Jews in Shushan gathered again on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred more men in Shushan, but again they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

¹⁶ Meanwhile, the rest of the Jews throughout the king's provinces had gathered to defend themselves. They gained relief from their enemies and killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them, though they did not touch the plunder. ¹⁷ This was on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar. On the fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness. ¹⁸ The Jews in Shushan, however, had assembled on both the thirteenth and fourteenth days, and they rested on the fifteenth day and made that a day of feasting and gladness. ¹⁹ That is why the rural Jews — those living in villages and unwalled towns — celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, making it a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday for giving gifts of food to one another. ²⁰ Mordecai recorded all these events and sent letters to all the Jews throughout the near and far provinces of King Ahasuerus,

²¹ calling on them to observe every year both the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar ²² as the days when the Jews got relief from their enemies, and as the month when their sorrow was turned into joy and their mourning into celebration. He told them to observe these days with feasting and gladness, giving gifts of food to one another and presenting gifts to the poor. ²³ So the Jews committed themselves to continuing what they had started, as Mordecai had written to them. ²⁴ For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them and had cast the Pur — that is, the lot — to crush and destroy them. ²⁵ But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by written decree that the evil scheme Haman had devised against the Jews should come back on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

²⁶ These days were called Purim, from the word Pur. Therefore, because of everything written in this letter — and because of what they themselves had witnessed and what had happened to them — ²⁷ the Jews established and committed themselves and their descendants and all who joined them to observe these two days every year without fail, in the way prescribed and at the time appointed. ²⁸ These days were to be remembered and observed in every generation, by every family, in every province, and in every city. The days of Purim would never cease to be observed among the Jews, and the memory of these events would never die out among their descendants. ²⁹ Then Queen Esther daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim. ³⁰ Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of Ahasuerus' kingdom — letters of peace and assurance —

³¹ to confirm the observance of these days of Purim at their designated times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had decreed, and as they had established for themselves and their descendants — including the obligations of fasting and mourning. ³² Esther's decree confirmed these regulations about Purim, and it was recorded in a book.

¹ King Ahasuerus imposed a tribute on the land and on the coastlands of the sea. ² All his acts of power and might, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai, whom the king had honored — are they not recorded in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia? ³ Mordecai the Jew stood second only to King Ahasuerus himself. He was great among the Jews, held in high esteem by his many compatriots, for he worked for the good of his people and spoke up for the welfare of all his descendants.

chapters.title: Job
paragraphs: ¹ In the land of Uz there lived a man named Job — a man of complete integrity who feared God and turned away from evil. ² He had seven sons and three daughters. ³ His wealth included seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred donkeys, and a large household of servants. He was the greatest man among all the people of the East. ⁴ His sons would take turns holding feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them. ⁵ When each round of feasting was over, Job would send for his children and consecrate them, rising early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for each one of them. He thought, "Perhaps my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." This was Job's regular practice.

⁶ One day the angels came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came with them. ⁷ The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered, "From roaming through the earth, going back and forth across it." ⁸ Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him — a man of complete integrity who fears God and turns away from evil." ⁹ Satan replied, "Does Job fear God for nothing? ¹⁰ Haven't you put a protective hedge around him and his household and everything he owns? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his flocks and herds have spread throughout the land."

¹¹ "But now reach out your hand and strike everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face." ¹² The LORD said to Satan, "Very well, everything he has is in your power — but do not lay a hand on the man himself." So Satan left the presence of the LORD. ¹³ One day when Job's sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother's house, ¹⁴ a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby, ¹⁵ when the Sabeans attacked and seized them. They cut down all the servants with the sword — I alone escaped to tell you."

¹⁶ While this messenger was still speaking, another arrived and said, "Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants, consuming them all — I alone escaped to tell you." ¹⁷ While he was still speaking, yet another messenger arrived and said, "The Chaldeans formed three raiding parties and swept down on your camels, carrying them off and killing all the servants with the sword — I alone escaped to tell you." ¹⁸ While this one was still speaking, another came and said, "Your sons and daughters were feasting and drinking wine at the oldest brother's house, ¹⁹ when suddenly a great wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on them, and they are all dead — I alone escaped to tell you." ²⁰ At this, Job got up, tore his robe, shaved his head, and fell to the ground in worship.

²¹ He said, "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I will depart. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away — blessed be the name of the LORD." ²² In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with any wrongdoing.

¹ On another day the angels came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came with them to present himself before him. ² The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered, "From roaming through the earth, going back and forth across it." ³ Then the LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job? There is no one on earth like him — a man of complete integrity who fears God and turns away from evil. And he still holds fast to his integrity, even though you incited me against him to ruin him without cause." ⁴ Satan replied, "Skin for skin! A man will give everything he has to save his own life. ⁵ But stretch out your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse you to your face."

⁶ The LORD said to Satan, "Very well — he is in your hands, but spare his life." ⁷ So Satan left the presence of the LORD and afflicted Job with terrible sores from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head. ⁸ Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself, and he sat down among the ashes. ⁹ His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your integrity? Curse God and die!" ¹⁰ He replied, "You're talking like a foolish woman. Shall we accept good from God and not trouble?" In all this, Job did not sin in what he said.

¹¹ When Job's three friends — Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite — heard about all the calamity that had come upon him, they set out from their homes and met together by agreement to go and sympathize with him and comfort him. ¹² When they saw him from a distance, they could barely recognize him. They wept aloud, tore their robes, and threw dust on their heads toward heaven. ¹³ Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word, because they saw how overwhelming his suffering was.

¹ After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth. ² He said: ³ "May the day I was born be destroyed, and the night it was announced, 'A boy is conceived.' ⁴ May that day be darkness — may God above not seek it out, nor any light shine on it. ⁵ May darkness and deep shadow claim it; may a cloud settle over it; may blackness overwhelm its light.

⁶ As for that night — may thick darkness seize it; may it not be included among the days of the year or counted among the months. ⁷ May that night be barren; may no shout of joy be heard in it. ⁸ May those who curse the day curse it — those skilled at rousing Leviathan. ⁹ May its morning stars turn dark; may it wait in vain for the light of dawn, never seeing the first rays of sunrise — ¹⁰ because it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb and hide trouble from my eyes.

¹¹ Why did I not die at birth? Why did I not perish as I came from the womb? ¹² Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts to nurse me? ¹³ If only I had never come into being, or had been carried straight from the womb to the grave. ¹⁴ I would now be lying in peaceful sleep, at rest with kings and rulers of the earth who built themselves places now lying in ruins, ¹⁵ or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.

¹⁶ Or why was I not buried like a stillborn child — like an infant who never saw the light of day? ¹⁷ There the wicked cease their troubling, and there the weary find rest. ¹⁸ There the prisoners rest together, no longer hearing the voice of the oppressor. ¹⁹ The small and the great are there alike, and the slave is free from his master. ²⁰ Why is light given to those who are in misery, and life to the bitter in soul,

²¹ who long for death that does not come, and search for it more eagerly than for hidden treasure? ²² How glad they would be, how they would rejoice, to reach the grave at last! ²³ Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in? ²⁴ For my groaning comes before I eat; my anguish pours out like water. ²⁵ What I feared has come upon me; what I dreaded has overtaken me.
²⁶ I have no peace, no quietness; I have no rest — only turmoil.

¹ Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied: ² "If someone tries to speak with you, will you be impatient? But who can keep from speaking? ³ Think of how you have instructed many and have strengthened feeble hands. ⁴ Your words have steadied those who were falling, and you have strengthened trembling knees. ⁵ But now trouble has come to you, and you are overwhelmed; it strikes you, and you fall apart.

⁶ "Should not your reverence for God give you confidence? Should not your blameless ways be your hope? ⁷ Think carefully — has the innocent ever perished? Has the upright ever been destroyed? ⁸ What I have seen is this: those who plow evil and sow trouble reap the same. ⁹ They perish by the breath of God; they are consumed by the blast of his anger. ¹⁰ The roar of the lion, the growl of the great lion — even the teeth of the young lions are broken.

¹¹ The mighty lion perishes for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness scatter. ¹² Now a word was secretly brought to me; my ear caught a whisper of it. ¹³ It came to me in disturbing visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people. ¹⁴ Fear and trembling seized me and made all my bones shake. ¹⁵ A spirit glided past my face, and the hair on my body stood on end.

¹⁶ It stopped, but I could not make out its form; a shape was before my eyes, and I heard a hushed voice: ¹⁷ 'Can a mortal be more righteous than God? Can even a strong man be more pure than his Maker? ¹⁸ If God places no trust in his servants, if he charges his angels with error, ¹⁹ how much more those who live in houses of clay, whose foundations are in the dust, who are crushed more easily than a moth! ²⁰ Between dawn and dusk they are shattered; unnoticed, they perish forever.
²¹ Are not the tent cords of their life pulled up? They die without ever gaining wisdom.'

¹ Call out now — is there anyone who will answer you? Which of the holy ones will you turn to? ² Resentment kills a fool, and envy slays the simpleton. ³ I myself have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly his house was cursed. ⁴ His children are far from safety; they are crushed in the city gate, with no one to rescue them. ⁵ Their harvest is eaten by the hungry, who take it even from among the thorns; the thirsty swallow up their wealth.

⁶ For hardship does not grow from the soil, nor does trouble spring from the ground. ⁷ Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward. ⁸ But if I were you, I would appeal to God and lay my cause before him — ⁹ the one who does great things beyond our understanding, wonders beyond all counting, ¹⁰ who gives rain to the earth and sends water on the fields,

¹¹ who sets the lowly on high and lifts the mourners to safety. ¹² He foils the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands accomplish nothing. ¹³ He catches the wise in their own cunning, and the plans of the devious are swept away. ¹⁴ Darkness overtakes them in broad daylight; at noon they grope as though it were night. ¹⁵ He saves the needy from the sword in their mouths and from the clutches of the powerful.

¹⁶ So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth. ¹⁷ Blessed is the one whom God corrects — so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty. ¹⁸ For he wounds, and he binds up; he injures, and his hands also heal. ¹⁹ From six calamities he will rescue you; in seven no harm will touch you. ²⁰ In famine he will deliver you from death, and in battle from the stroke of the sword.

²¹ You will be sheltered from the lash of the tongue, and need not fear when destruction comes. ²² You will laugh at destruction and famine, and need not be afraid of the beasts of the earth. ²³ For you will have an agreement with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you. ²⁴ You will know that your tent is secure; you will take stock of your property and find nothing missing. ²⁵ You will know that your children will be many, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
²⁶ You will come to the grave in full vigor, like grain that is gathered in season. ²⁷ We have examined this thoroughly, and it is true. Hear it, and apply it to yourself.

¹ Then Job replied: ² "If only my anguish could be weighed and all my misery placed on the scales! ³ It would surely outweigh the sand of the seas — no wonder my words have been rash. ⁴ The arrows of the Almighty have pierced me; my spirit drinks in their poison; God's terrors are marshaled against me. ⁵ Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass? Does an ox bellow when it has feed?

⁶ Can bland food be eaten without salt? Is there any taste in the white of an egg? ⁷ My appetite refuses to touch such things; they are like disgusting food to me. ⁸ Oh, that I might have what I ask for, that God would grant what I hope for — ⁹ that he would be willing to crush me, to let loose his hand and cut me off! ¹⁰ Then I would still have this comfort, this joy even in relentless pain: that I had not denied the words of the Holy One.

¹¹ What strength do I have to go on hoping? What future awaits me that I should be patient? ¹² Is my strength the strength of stone? Is my body made of iron? ¹³ Do I have any power to help myself, now that every resource has been driven from me? ¹⁴ A desperate man should have the devotion of his friends, even if he abandons the fear of the Almighty. ¹⁵ But my brothers have been as treacherous as a seasonal stream, as the courses of streams that run dry,

¹⁶ dark from melting ice and swollen with snowmelt, ¹⁷ but that vanish in the heat and disappear in the warmth. ¹⁸ Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go up into the wasteland and perish. ¹⁹ The caravans of Tema look for water; the traveling merchants of Sheba hope to find it. ²⁰ They are disappointed because they had been confident; they arrived there only to be let down.

²¹ Now you too have proved to be nothing — you see something dreadful and you pull back in fear. ²² Have I ever said, 'Give me something'? Have I asked you, 'Pay a bribe on my behalf'? ²³ Or, 'Rescue me from the hand of the enemy'? Or, 'Deliver me from the grip of ruthless men'? ²⁴ Teach me, and I will be silent; show me where I have been wrong. ²⁵ How painful honest words can be! But what do your arguments prove?

²⁶ Do you think you can reprove my words as though they were just wind? You would even cast lots for the fatherless and make merchandise of your own friend. ²⁷ Are you plotting to criticize me? Would you even cast lots over an orphan and barter away your friend? ²⁸ But now please look at me — would I lie to your face? ²⁹ Relent, do not be unjust; reconsider, for my integrity is at stake. ³⁰ Is there any injustice on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern wickedness?

¹ Is not a person forced to labor on earth? Are not their days like those of a hired worker? ² Like a slave longing for shade, like a hired worker waiting to be paid, ³ so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery have been measured out for me. ⁴ When I lie down I think, 'How long before I get up?' The night drags on, and I toss and turn until dawn. ⁵ My body is clothed in worms and scabs; my skin is cracked and covered with sores.

⁶ My days fly by faster than a weaver's shuttle and come to an end without hope. ⁷ Remember, O God, that my life is but a breath; my eyes will never see happiness again. ⁸ The eye that now sees me will see me no more; your eyes will look for me, but I will be gone. ⁹ As a cloud vanishes and is gone, so one who goes down to the grave does not return. ¹⁰ He will never come home again; his place will know him no more.

¹¹ Therefore I will not keep silent; I will speak out in the anguish of my spirit, I will complain in the bitterness of my soul. ¹² Am I the sea, or the monster of the deep, that you put me under guard? ¹³ When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaints, ¹⁴ you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions, ¹⁵ so that I prefer strangling — death itself rather than this body of mine.

¹⁶ I despise my life; I would not live forever. Leave me alone — my days mean nothing. ¹⁷ What is mankind that you make so much of them, that you give them so much attention? ¹⁸ That you examine them every morning and test them every moment? ¹⁹ Will you never look away from me, or let me alone even for an instant? ²⁰ If I have sinned, what have I done to you, O watcher of all humanity? Why have you made me your target? Have I become a burden to you?
²¹ Why do you not pardon my offenses and forgive my sins? For I will soon lie down in the dust; you will search for me, but I will be no more."

¹ Then Bildad the Shuhite replied: ² "How long will you go on talking like this? Your words are a blustering wind. ³ Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty distort what is right? ⁴ When your children sinned against him, he gave them over to the penalty of their sin. ⁵ But if you seek God earnestly and plead with the Almighty,

⁶ if you are pure and upright, even now he will rouse himself on your behalf and restore you to your rightful place. ⁷ Your beginnings will seem humble, so prosperous will your future be. ⁸ Ask the former generation; pay attention to what their ancestors learned — ⁹ for we were born only yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are but a shadow. ¹⁰ Will they not instruct you and tell you? Will they not bring forth words from their understanding?

¹¹ Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh? Can reeds thrive without water? ¹² While still growing and uncut, they wither more quickly than grass. ¹³ Such is the fate of all who forget God; so perishes the hope of the godless. ¹⁴ What they trust in is fragile; what they rely on is a spider's web. ¹⁵ They lean on the web, but it gives way; they cling to it, but it does not hold.

¹⁶ They are like a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden. ¹⁷ It entwines its roots around a pile of rocks and looks for a place among the stones. ¹⁸ But when it is torn from its spot, that place disowns it and says, 'I never saw you.' ¹⁹ Surely its life withers away, and from the soil other plants grow. ²⁰ Surely God does not reject one who is blameless, nor does he lend his support to the wicked.
²¹ He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy. ²² Your enemies will be clothed in shame, and the tents of the wicked will be no more."

¹ Then Job replied: ² "Yes, I know what you say is true — but how can mere mortals prove their innocence before God? ³ Though they wished to dispute with him, they could not answer him one time out of a thousand. ⁴ His wisdom is profound, his power is vast. Who has resisted him and come out unscathed? ⁵ He moves mountains without their knowing it and overturns them in his anger.

⁶ He shakes the earth from its place and makes its pillars tremble. ⁷ He speaks to the sun and it does not shine; he seals off the light of the stars. ⁸ He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the waves of the sea. ⁹ He made the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the constellations of the south. ¹⁰ He performs wonders that cannot be fathomed, miracles that cannot be counted.

¹¹ When he passes me, I cannot see him; when he goes by, I cannot perceive him. ¹² If he snatches something away, who can stop him? Who can say to him, 'What are you doing?' ¹³ God does not restrain his anger; even the allies of Rahab cowered at his feet. ¹⁴ How then can I dispute with him? How can I find words to argue with him? ¹⁵ Even if I were innocent, I could not answer him; I could only plead with my Judge for mercy.

¹⁶ Even if I summoned him and he responded, I do not believe he would give me a hearing. ¹⁷ He would crush me with a storm and multiply my wounds for no reason. ¹⁸ He would not let me catch my breath but would overwhelm me with misery. ¹⁹ If it is a matter of strength, he is mighty! And if it is a matter of justice, who can challenge him? ²⁰ Even if I were innocent, my mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would prove me guilty.

²¹ Although I am blameless, I have no concern for myself; I despise my own life. ²² It is all the same — that is why I say, 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.' ²³ When a plague brings sudden death, he mocks the despair of the innocent. ²⁴ When a land falls into the hands of the wicked, he blindfolds its judges. If it is not he, then who is it? ²⁵ My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away without a glimpse of joy.

²⁶ They are gone like swift ships, like an eagle diving on its prey. ²⁷ If I say, "I will put my grief aside, I will set down my sorrow and find some comfort" — ²⁸ I am terrified by all my suffering, for I know you will not clear me of guilt. ²⁹ If I am already condemned, why should I struggle for nothing? ³⁰ Even if I scrubbed myself with snow and cleansed my hands with lye, ³¹ you would plunge me into a pit, and my own clothes would recoil from me.

³² He is not a man like me, that I could answer him, that we could stand together before a court. ³³ There is no one to mediate between us, no one who could lay his hand on us both. ³⁴ Let him take his rod away from me, let his terror no longer overwhelm me — ³⁵ then I would speak without fear, for that is not how I am in myself.

¹ My soul is sick of life. I will pour out my complaint freely; I will speak from the bitterness of my soul. ² I will say to God, "Do not condemn me — show me why you are contending with me. ³ Does it please you to oppress me, to despise the work of your own hands, while you smile on the schemes of the wicked? ⁴ Do you see as a mortal sees? Do you look on things the way humans do? ⁵ Are your days like the days of a man, your years like a man's years,

⁶ that you must search out my sin and seek out my wrongdoing? ⁷ You know that I am not guilty, and no one can rescue me from your hand. ⁸ Your own hands shaped me and made me — and now you turn and destroy me? ⁹ Remember that you formed me like clay. Will you return me to dust? ¹⁰ Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?

¹¹ You clothed me with skin and flesh, you knit me together with bones and sinews. ¹² You gave me life and showed me steadfast love, and your care has preserved my spirit. ¹³ Yet these things you hid in your heart — I know this was your purpose all along. ¹⁴ If I sinned, you would be watching, and you would not let my guilt go unpunished. ¹⁵ If I am wicked, then woe to me; and even if I am righteous, I dare not lift my head — I am so filled with shame, soaked in my own misery.

¹⁶ And if I hold my head up, you hunt me like a fierce lion, and turn your power against me once more. ¹⁷ You bring fresh witnesses against me, and your anger toward me grows — blow after blow, wave after wave of assault. ¹⁸ Then why did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before any eye had seen me, ¹⁹ that I had been carried from the womb to the grave, as though I had never existed. ²⁰ The few days of my life are almost spent — leave me alone, let me have a little comfort

²¹ before I go to the place I will never return from — the land of darkness and the shadow of death, ²² a land as dark as the darkness itself, where the shadow of death covers all, where there is no order, and where the light is as dark as night.

¹ Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said: ² "Should all these words go unanswered? Should a man who talks so much be proved right? ³ Should your empty words silence everyone? Should you mock, and no one call you out? ⁴ You claim your beliefs are sound, that you are pure in God's eyes. ⁵ But if only God would speak, if only he would open his lips against you,

⁶ and tell you the secrets of wisdom — for true wisdom has two sides. Know this: God is not even holding you fully accountable for all your wrongdoing. ⁷ Can you fathom the depths of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty? ⁸ They are higher than the heavens — what can you do? Deeper than the grave — what can you know? ⁹ Their measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea. ¹⁰ If he passes through and puts someone in prison, or calls a court to order, who can stop him?

Have you clothed its neck with a flowing mane? ²⁰ Can you make it leap like a locust? Its proud snorting is terrifying!

²¹ It paws the ground in the valley, exulting in its strength; it charges into battle. ²² It laughs at fear and is not frightened; it does not shy away from the sword. ²³ The quiver rattles against its side, the flashing spear and javelin. ²⁴ With fierce energy it devours the ground; it cannot stand still when the battle trumpet sounds. ²⁵ At each blast of the horn it snorts, 'Aha!' It catches the scent of battle from afar, the thunder of commanders and the battle cry.

²⁶ Is it by your wisdom that the hawk takes flight and spreads its wings toward the south? ²⁷ Does the eagle soar at your command and build its nest on high? ²⁸ It dwells on the rocky crag, on the steep face of rock and cliff. ²⁹ From there it hunts for food; its eyes scan the distant horizon. ³⁰ Its young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there it is."

¹ The LORD said to Job: ² "Will the one who argues with the Almighty correct him? Let the one who accuses God give him an answer." ³ Then Job replied to the LORD: ⁴ "I am unworthy — how can I reply to you? I put my hand over my mouth. ⁵ I spoke once, but I have no answer; twice, but I will say no more."

⁶ Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind: ⁷ "Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will answer me. ⁸ Would you discredit my justice? Would you condemn me to justify yourself? ⁹ Do you have an arm like God's? Can your voice thunder like his? ¹⁰ Then adorn yourself with glory and splendor; clothe yourself with honor and majesty.

¹¹ Unleash the fury of your wrath; look at all who are proud and bring them low. ¹² Look at all who are proud and humble them; crush the wicked where they stand. ¹³ Bury them all in the dust together; shroud their faces in the grave. ¹⁴ Then I myself will admit to you that your own right hand can save you.

¹⁶ Look at Behemoth, which I made along with you — it feeds on grass like an ox. ¹⁷ What power it has in its loins, what strength in the muscles of its belly! ¹⁸ Its tail sways like a cedar; the sinews of its thighs are tightly knit. ¹⁹ Its bones are like beams of bronze; its limbs like rods of iron. ²⁰ It is the chief of God's works; yet its Maker can approach it with his sword.

²¹ It lies under the lotus plants, hidden among the reeds in the marsh. ²² The lotuses conceal it in their shadow; the poplars along the stream surround it. ²³ When the river rages, it is not alarmed; it remains calm though the Jordan rushes against its mouth. ²⁴ Can anyone capture it by the eyes, or trap it and pierce its nose?

¹ "Can you pull in Leviathan with a fishhook, or tie down its tongue with a rope? ² Can you put a cord through its nose, or pierce its jaw with a hook? ³ Will it keep begging you for mercy? Will it speak gentle words to you? ⁴ Will it make a covenant with you to become your servant for life? ⁵ Can you make it a pet like a bird, or put it on a leash for your girls?

⁶ Will a band of merchants try to buy it? Will they divide it up among the traders? ⁷ Can you fill its hide with harpoons, or its head with fishing spears? ⁸ Lay your hand on it — you will remember the battle and never do it again! ⁹ Look — the hope of attacking it is futile; even the sight of it is overwhelming.

¹¹ Who dares oppose me and come out alive? Everything under heaven is mine. ¹² I will not fail to speak of Leviathan's limbs, its strength, and its graceful proportions. ¹³ Who can strip off its outer coat? Who can penetrate its double coat of armor? ¹⁴ Who can open the doors of its mouth, ringed with fearsome teeth? ¹⁵ Its back has rows of shields locked tightly together as with a seal.

¹⁶ Each is so close to the next that no air can pass between them. ¹⁷ They are joined to one another; they lock together and cannot be pulled apart. ¹⁸ Its snorting flashes with light; its eyes are like the glimmer of dawn. ¹⁹ Flames stream from its mouth; sparks of fire shoot out. ²⁰ Smoke pours from its nostrils as from a boiling pot heated over rushes.

²¹ Its breath sets coals ablaze; flames dart from its mouth. ²² Strength lodges in its neck; dismay goes before it. ²³ The folds of its flesh are tightly joined; they are firm and immovable. ²⁴ Its chest is hard as rock, hard as a lower millstone. ²⁵ When it rises up, the mighty are terrified; they fall back before its thrashing.

²⁶ The sword that strikes it cannot hold; nor can spear, dart, or javelin. ²⁷ Iron it treats like straw and bronze like rotten wood. ²⁸ Arrows do not make it flee; slingstones are like chaff to it. ²⁹ A club seems to it a piece of straw; it laughs at the rattling of the lance. ³⁰ Its underside is jagged shards; it moves across the mud like a threshing sledge.

³¹ It makes the depths churn like a boiling cauldron; it stirs up the sea like a pot of ointment. ³² It leaves a glistening wake behind it; one would think the deep had turned white. ³³ Nothing on earth is its equal — a creature without fear. ³⁴ It looks down on all that are haughty; it is king over all that are proud."

¹ Then Job replied to the LORD: ² "I know that you can do all things; no purpose of yours can be thwarted. ³ You asked, 'Who is this who obscures my plans without knowledge?' Surely I spoke of things I did not understand — things too wonderful for me to know. ⁴ You said, 'Listen now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.' ⁵ My ears had heard of you, but now my eyes have seen you.

⁶ Therefore I retract what I said, and I repent in dust and ashes. ⁷ After the LORD had said these things to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "My anger burns against you and your two friends, because you have not spoken the truth about me, as my servant Job has. ⁸ So now take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job and sacrifice a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly. You have not spoken the truth about me, as my servant Job has." ⁹ So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite did what the LORD told them; and the LORD accepted Job's prayer. ¹⁰ After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his fortunes and gave him twice as much as he had before.

¹¹ All his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came and ate with him in his house. They comforted and consoled him over all the trouble the LORD had brought on him, and each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring. ¹² The LORD blessed the latter part of Job's life more than the former. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand donkeys. ¹³ And he also had seven sons and three daughters. ¹⁴ The first daughter he named Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-Happuch. ¹⁵ Nowhere in all the land were there found women as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father granted them an inheritance along with their brothers.
¹⁶ After this, Job lived a hundred and forty years; he saw his children and their children to the fourth generation. ¹⁷ And so Job died — old and full of years.

chapters.title: Proverbs
paragraphs: ¹ The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel: ² for learning wisdom and discipline, for understanding words of insight, ³ for gaining a disciplined and prudent life, doing what is right and just and fair; ⁴ for giving wisdom to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young — ⁵ let the wise listen and add to their learning, and let the discerning get guidance —

⁶ for understanding proverbs and parables, the sayings and riddles of the wise. ⁷ The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline. ⁸ My son, listen to your father's instruction and do not forsake your mother's teaching. ⁹ They are a garland to grace your head and a chain to adorn your neck. ¹⁰ My son, if sinners try to entice you, do not give in to them.

¹¹ If they say, "Come along with us; let's lie in wait for someone's blood, let's ambush some harmless soul; ¹² let's swallow them alive, like the grave, and whole, like those who go down to the pit; ¹³ we will get all kinds of valuable things and fill our houses with plunder; ¹⁴ throw in your lot with us, and we will share a common purse" — ¹⁵ my son, do not go along with them; keep your feet from their path;

¹⁶ for their feet rush into evil, they are quick to shed blood. ¹⁷ How futile to spread a net in full view of all the birds! ¹⁸ These men lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush only themselves. ¹⁹ Such is the end of all who go after ill-gotten gain; it takes away the life of those who get it. ²⁰ Out in the open wisdom calls aloud; she raises her voice in the public square.

²¹ She cries out above the noise of the crowd; at the entrance to the city gates she makes her speech: ²² "How long will you who are simple love your simple ways? How long will mockers delight in mockery and fools hate knowledge? ²³ Repent at my rebuke! Then I will pour out my thoughts to you; I will make known to you my teachings.

²⁶ I in turn will laugh when disaster strikes you; I will mock when calamity overtakes you — ²⁷ when calamity sweeps over you like a storm, when disaster rolls over you like a whirlwind, when distress and trouble overwhelm you. ²⁸ Then they will call to me but I will not answer; they will look for me but will not find me, ²⁹ since they hated knowledge and did not choose to fear the LORD. ³⁰ Since they would not accept my advice and spurned my rebuke,

³¹ they will eat the fruit of their ways and be filled with the fruit of their own schemes. ³² For the waywardness of the simple will kill them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them; ³³ but whoever listens to me will live in safety and be at ease, without fear of harm."

¹ My son, if you accept my words and store up my commands within you, ² turning your ear to wisdom and applying your heart to understanding — ³ indeed, if you call out for insight and cry aloud for understanding, ⁴ and if you look for it as for silver and search for it as for hidden treasure, ⁵ then you will understand the fear of the LORD and find the knowledge of God.

⁶ For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding. ⁷ He holds success in store for the upright; he is a shield to those whose walk is blameless, ⁸ for he guards the course of the just and protects the way of his faithful ones. ⁹ Then you will understand what is right and just and fair — every good path. ¹⁰ For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.

¹¹ Discretion will protect you, and understanding will guard you. ¹² Wisdom will save you from the ways of wicked men, from men whose words are perverse, ¹³ who have left the straight paths to walk in dark ways, ¹⁴ who delight in doing wrong and rejoice in the perverseness of evil, ¹⁵ whose paths are crooked and who are devious in their ways.

¹⁶ Wisdom will save you also from the adulterous woman, from the wayward woman with her seductive words, ¹⁷ who has left the partner of her youth and ignored the covenant she made before God. ¹⁸ Surely her house leads down to death and her paths to the spirits of the dead. ¹⁹ None who go to her return or attain the paths of life. ²⁰ Thus you will walk in the ways of the good and keep to the paths of the righteous.
²¹ For the upright will live in the land, and the blameless will remain in it; ²² but the wicked will be cut off from the land, and the unfaithful will be torn from it.

¹ My son, do not forget my teaching, but keep my commands in your heart, ² for they will prolong your life many years and bring you peace and prosperity. ³ Let love and faithfulness never leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart. ⁴ Then you will win favor and a good name in the sight of God and man. ⁵ Trust in the LORD with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding;

⁶ in all your ways submit to him, and he will make your paths straight. ⁷ Do not be wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and shun evil. ⁸ This will bring health to your body and nourishment to your bones. ⁹ Honor the LORD with your wealth, with the firstfruits of all your crops; ¹⁰ then your barns will be filled to overflowing, and your vats will brim over with new wine.

¹¹ My son, do not despise the LORD's discipline, and do not resent his rebuke, ¹² because the LORD disciplines those he loves, as a father the son he delights in. ¹³ Blessed are those who find wisdom, those who gain understanding, ¹⁴ for she is more profitable than silver and yields better returns than gold. ¹⁵ She is more precious than rubies; nothing you desire can compare with her.

¹⁶ Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor. ¹⁷ Her ways are pleasant ways, and all her paths are peace. ¹⁸ She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her; those who hold her fast will be blessed. ¹⁹ By wisdom the LORD laid the earth's foundations, by understanding he set the heavens in place; ²⁰ by his knowledge the watery depths were divided, and the clouds let drop the dew.

²¹ My son, do not let wisdom and understanding out of your sight; preserve sound judgment and discretion; ²² they will be life for you, an ornament to grace your neck. ²³ Then you will go on your way in safety, and your foot will not stumble. ²⁴ When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you lie down, your sleep will be sweet. ²⁵ Have no fear of sudden disaster or of the ruin that overtakes the wicked,

²⁶ for the LORD will be at your side and will keep your foot from being snared. ²⁷ Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act. ²⁸ Do not say to your neighbor, "Come back tomorrow and I'll give it to you" — when you already have it with you. ²⁹ Do not plot harm against your neighbor, who lives trustfully near you. ³⁰ Do not accuse anyone for no reason — when they have done you no harm.

³¹ Do not envy the violent or choose any of their ways. ³² For the LORD detests the perverse but takes the upright into his confidence. ³³ The LORD's curse is on the house of the wicked, but he blesses the home of the righteous. ³⁴ He mocks proud mockers but shows favor to the humble and oppressed. ³⁵ The wise inherit honor, but fools get only shame.

¹ Listen, my sons, to a father's instruction; pay attention and gain understanding. ² I give you sound learning, so do not forsake my teaching. ³ For I too was a son to my father, still tender, and cherished by my mother. ⁴ Then he taught me, and he said to me, "Take hold of my words with all your heart; keep my commands, and you will live. ⁵ Get wisdom, get understanding; do not forget my words or turn away from them.

⁶ Do not forsake wisdom, and she will protect you; love her, and she will watch over you. ⁷ The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom. Though it cost all you have, get understanding. ⁸ Cherish her, and she will exalt you; embrace her, and she will honor you. ⁹ She will give you a garland to grace your head and present you with a glorious crown." ¹⁰ Listen, my son, accept what I say, and the years of your life will be many.

¹¹ I instruct you in the way of wisdom and lead you along straight paths. ¹² When you walk, your steps will not be hampered; when you run, you will not stumble. ¹³ Hold on to instruction, do not let it go; guard it well, for it is your life. ¹⁴ Do not set foot on the path of the wicked or walk in the way of evildoers. ¹⁵ Avoid it, do not travel on it; turn from it and go on your way.

¹⁶ For they cannot rest until they do evil; they are robbed of sleep till they make someone stumble. ¹⁷ They eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence. ¹⁸ The path of the righteous is like the morning sun, shining ever brighter till the full light of day. ¹⁹ But the way of the wicked is like deep darkness; they do not know what makes them stumble. ²⁰ My son, pay attention to what I say; turn your ear to my words.

²¹ Do not let them out of your sight; keep them within your heart; ²² for they are life to those who find them and health to one's whole body. ²³ Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it. ²⁴ Keep your mouth free of perversity; keep corrupt talk far from your lips. ²⁵ Let your eyes look straight ahead; fix your gaze directly before you.
²⁶ Give careful thought to the paths for your feet and be steadfast in all your ways. ²⁷ Do not turn to the right or the left; keep your foot from evil.

¹ My son, pay attention to my wisdom, turn your ear to my words of insight, ² that you may maintain discretion and your lips may preserve knowledge. ³ For the lips of the adulterous woman drip honey, and her speech is smoother than oil; ⁴ but in the end she is bitter as gall, sharp as a double-edged sword. ⁵ Her feet go down to death; her steps lead straight to the grave.

⁶ She gives no thought to the way of life; her paths wander aimlessly, but she does not know it. ⁷ Now then, my sons, listen to me; do not turn aside from what I say. ⁸ Keep to a path far from her; do not go near the door of her house, ⁹ lest you lose your honor to others and your dignity to one who is cruel, ¹⁰ lest strangers feast on your wealth and your toil enrich the house of another.

¹¹ At the end of your life you will groan, when your flesh and body are spent. ¹² You will say, "How I hated discipline! How my heart spurned correction! ¹³ I would not obey my teachers or turn my ear to my instructors. ¹⁴ And I was soon in serious trouble in the assembly of God's people." ¹⁵ Drink water from your own cistern, running water from your own well.

¹⁶ Should your springs overflow in the streets, your streams of water in the public squares? ¹⁷ Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers. ¹⁸ May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth. ¹⁹ A loving doe, a graceful deer — may her breasts satisfy you always, may you ever be intoxicated with her love. ²⁰ Why, my son, be intoxicated with another man's wife? Why embrace the bosom of a wayward woman?
